A MESSAGE from His Majesty, by Sir Francis Molyneux, Gentleman Usher of the Black Rod t

Mr. Speaker*

The King commands this Honourable Houseto attend His Majesty, immediately, in the House of Peers.

Accordingly Mr. Speaker, with the House, went up to attend His Majesty:

And being returned;

A Member present, and several Members returned upon new Writs, took the Oaths of Allegiance and Supremacy, and made and subscribed the Declaration, and took and subscribed the Oath of Abjuration, according to the Laws made for those Purposes; and such of the said Members as are by Law required to deliver in, to the Clerk of this House, an Account of their Qualification, and to take and subscribe the Oath of Qualification, delivered in such Account, and took and subscribed the said Oath accordingly.

A Bill for the more effectual preventing Clartdestine Outlawries, was read the First Time.

Resolved, That the Bill be read a Second Time.

Mr. Speaker reported, That the House had attended His Majesty in the House of Peers; where His Majesty was pleased to make a most Gracious Speech from the Throne to both Houses of Parliament; of which Mr. Speaker said, he had, to prevent Mistakes, obtained a Copy; which he read to the House, and is as followeth; viz.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

1 have the Satisfaction to acquaint you, that the

important Negotiations, in which I was engaged at the Close of the last Session of Parliament, are brought to a favourable Conclusion. The Differences with the Northern Powers have been adjusted by a Convention with the Emperor of Russia, to which the Kings of Denmark and Sweden have expressed their Readiness to accede. The essential Rights for which We contended are thereby secured; and Provision is made, that the Exercise of them shall be attended with as little Molestation as possible to the Subjects of the contracting Parties.

VOL. 57.

Preliminaries of Peace have also been ratified between Me and the French Republick; and I trust that this important Arrangement, whilst it manifests the Justice and Moderation of My Views, will also be found conducive to the substantial Interests of this Country, and honourable to the RritijhCharacter: — Copies of these

Papers shall forthwith belaid before you; and I e&rneftly hope that the Transactions to which they refer will meet with the Approbation of My Parliament.

Gentlemen of the House of Commons,

I have directed such Estimates to be prepared of the various Demands for the Public Service as appear to Me to be best adapted to the Situation in which We are now placed. It is painful to Me to reflect, that Provision cannot be made for defraying the Expences which must unavoidably be continued, for a Time, in different. Parts of the World, and for maintaining an adequate Peace Establishment, without large additional Supplies. You may, however, be assured, that all possible Attention shall be paid to such ceconomical Arrangements as may not be inconsistent with the great Object of effectually providing for the Security of all My Dominions.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

I cannot sufficiently describe the Gratification and Comfort I derive from the Relief, which the Bounty of Divine Providence has afforded to My People, by the abundant Produce of the late Harvest: — In contemplating the Situation of the Country at this important Conjuncture, it is impossible for Me to refrain from expressing the deep Sense I entertain of the Temper and Fortitude, which have been manifested by all Descriptions of My faithful Subjects, under the various and complicated Difficulties with which they have had to contend.

The distinguislled Valour and eminent Services of My Forces by Sea and Land, which, at no Period* have been surpassed; the unprecedented Exertions of the Militia and Fencibles, and the Zeal and Perseverance of the Yeomanry and Volunteer Corps of Cavalry and Infantry, are entitled to My warmest Acknowledgements; and I am persuaded, that you will join with Me in reflecting, with peculiar Satisfaction, on the Naval and Military Operations of the last Campaign; and on the fucceisful and glorious Issue of the Expedition to Egypt, which has been marked throughout by Atchievements, tending, in their Consequences and by their Example, to produce lalling Advantage and Honour to this Country.

Kesolution for Ad tire Is on King'sSpccch.

4 29 — 3o°

It is My first Wish, and most fervent Prayer, that My People may experience the Reward they have so well merited, in a hill Enjoyment of the Blelfings of Peace, in a progressive Increase of the National Commerce, Credit, and Rel'ources; and, above all, in the undisturbed Possession of their Religion, Laws, and Liberties, under the Safeguard and Protection of that Constitution, which it has been the great Object of all Our Efforts to preserve, and which it is Our most sacred Duty to transmit, unimpaired, to Our Descendants.

Resolved, Nemine Contradicente, That an humble

Address be presented to His Majesty, To return His Majesty the Thanks of this House, for His most gracious Speech from the Throne:

To allure His Majesty, that we learn, with great Satisfaction, that the Differences with the Northern Powers have been adjusted by a Convention with the Emperor of Rufia, to which the Kings of Denmark and Sweden have expressed their Readinel's to accede; and that Preliminaries of Peace have been ratified between His Majesty and the French Republick:

That we acknowledge His Majesty's Goodness in having been pleased to direct Copies of these Treaties to be laid before us; and, to assure His Majesty, that we shall not fail to apply our immediate Attention to the important Transadiions to which they relate:

That we are fully sensible of the paternal Solicitude which leads His Majesty to regret the Necessity of large additional Supplies; but that, while we sincerely participate in that Sentiment, we feel the indispensible Duty of providing for the Expences which must, for a Time, be unavoidable in different Parts of the World, and of maintaining an adequate Establishment on the linal Restoration of Peace:

That we shall be anxious for the Adoption of all such eeconomical Arrangements, as may not be inconsistent with the great Object, which His Majesty has fb justly at Heart, of effectually providing for the Security of all His Majesty's Dominions:

That we truly participate in the Gratification, which His Majesty has so graciously been pleased to express, at the Relief which the Bounty of Divine Providence has afforded to His People, by the Abundance of the late Harvest; and we acknowledge, with the utmost Gratitude, His Majesty's gracious Acceptance and Approbation of the Proofs of that Temper and Fortitude, which have been manifested by all Descriptions of His Subjects, under the various and complicated Difficulties with which they have had to contend:

That we rcflect with Sentiments of just Exultation on the distinguished Valour and eminent Services of His Majesty's Forces by Sea and Land, which at no Period have been surpassed; and that we have contemplated with the utmost Satisfaction the unprecedented Exertions of the Militia and Fencibles, and the Zeal and Perseverance of the Yeomanry and Volunteer Corps of Cavalry and Infantry:

That we most heartily congratulate His Majesty on the Naval and Military Operations of the last Campaign, and on the glorious and successful Ifl'ue of the Expedition to Egypt, marked as it has been throughout by Achievements, which, in their Consequences and by their Example, cannot fail to conduce to the lasting Advantage and Honour of this Country:

That we cordially share in His Majesty's earnest Willies, that His Subjects may enjoy in their full Extent tire returning Blessings of Peace, in the progressive Increase of the National Commerce, Credit, and Revenues; and, above all, in the undisturbed Possession of their Religion, Laws, and Liberties, under the Safeguard and Protection of that Constitution which it has been the great Object of all our Efforts to preserve, and which it is our fixed Determination, as it is our most sacred Duty, to transmit, unimpaired, to our De-feendants.

A PETITION of the Prisoners confined for Debt in His Majesty's Gaol at Maidstone, in the County of Kent, was presented to the House, and read; Complaining of their Distress, and praying Relief.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the Gentlemen, Clergy, Freeholders, and other Inhabitants, of the County of Monmouth, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the present Method of felling Wheat, ancf other Grain, by Measure, in which no regular Standard is used, is productive of great Inconvenience and Deception, and renders it impossible to ascertain the real Price of such Wheat and Grain; and it is found to be impracticable, under the existing Laws, to guard against the Frauds practised in the Returns made to the Clerk of the Markets, and consequently the Magistrates are unable to fix the Assize of Bread from these Returns with any Cor-rectness, in Proportion to the real Average Price of Com; and that the Public in general fuller great Imposition by felling Potatoes and Turnips by Measure, and it would be attended with great Public Utility, and would tend much to remedy the Evils now experienced (particularly by the Poor) if Wheat and all other Kinds of Grain, Flour, Meal, and also Potatoes and Tumips, were sold by one fixed Weight instead of Measur: And therefore praying, that the House will take the above Evils into Consideration, and provide such Remedy as to them shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the

Table.

Ordered, That all Persons, who will question any Returns of Members to serve in Parliament, for any County, City, Borough, or Place, in that Part of the United Kingdom called Great Britain, do question the same within Fourteen Days next, and so within Fourteen Days next after any new Return shall be brought in; and that all Members, who are returned for Two or more Places in Great Britain, do make their Election by this Day Three Weeks for which of the Places they will serve, provided there be no Question upon the Return for that Place; and, if any Thing shall come in question touching the Return or Election of any Member, he is to withdraw during the Time the Matter is in Debate; and that all Members, returned upon Double Returns, do withdraw till their Returns are determined.

Resolved, That all Persons who will question any Returns of Members to serve iri Parliament for that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland, which have been, or may be, made to Writs already issued, or ordered to be issued, do question the same within Twenty-eight Days after the same shall have been, or shall be, respectively returned into the Office of the Clerk of the Crown in that Part of the United Kingdom called England.

Resolved, That all Persons who will question any Returns of Members to serve in Parliament for that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland, to Writs not already issued, or ordered to be issued, do question the same by presenting a Petition to this House within Fourteen Days next after the same shall have been brought into the Office of the Clerk of the Crown of that Part of the United Kingdom called England, or by lodging a Petition in the Office of the Clerk of the Crown in that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland within Fourteen Days next after the same shall have been brought into the said Office.

Resolved, That, when any such Petition shall have been lodged in the said Office of the Clerk of the Crown in that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland, within the Time before limited, the said Clerk shall forthwith make a Copy thereof, to be preserved in the said Office, and immediately thereupon shall transmit such original Petition (in the Method used in conveying Returns of Writs) to the Speaker of the House of Commons, to be by him laid before the House: and that, in case no such Petition shall have been lodged in the said Office, within the Time before limited, the said Clerk of the Crown shall forthwith transmit a Certificate, in the like Manner, to the Speaker of the House of Commons, signed by himself, or his Deputy, specifying the Time

VOL. 57.

when such Return was made, and that no such Petition had been lodged in his Office previous to the Date of such Certificate.

A Motion was made, and the Question being proposed. That no Peer of this Realm hath any Right to give his Vote in the Election of any Member to serve in Parliament;

And a Debate arising in the House thereupon;

Ordered, That the Debate be adjourned till Monday Morning next.

A Motion was made, and the Question being proposed. That no Peer of Ireland, unless actually elected and serving for any County, City, or Borough, of Great Britain, hath any Right to give his Vote in the Election of any Member to serve in Parliament for that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland;

And a Debate arising in the House thereupon;

Ordered, That the Debate be adjourned till Monday Morifing next.

A Motion was made, and the Question being proposed. That no Peer of Ireland elected (or who shall be elected) to fit and vote on the Part of Ireland in the House of Lords of the Parliament of the United Kingdom, or who hath, or shall have voted at such Election, hath any Right to give his Vote in the Election of any Member to serve in Parliament for that Part of the United Kingdom called Great Britain;

And a Debate arising in the House thereupon;

Ordered, That the Debate be adjourned till Monday Morning next.

Resolved, That, if it shall appear that any Person hath procured himself to be elected or returned a Member of this House, or endeavoured so to be, by Bribery, or any other corrupt Practices, this House will proceed with the utmost Severity against such Person.

Resolved, That, if it shall appear that any Person hath been tampering with any Witness, in respect of his Evidence to be given to this House, or any Committee thereof, or directly or indirectly hath endeavoured to deter or hinder any Person from appearing, or giving Evidence, the same is declared to be a High Crime and Misdemeanor; and this House will proceed with the utmost Severity against such Offender.

Resolved, That, if it shall appear that any Person hath given false Evidence, in any Case, before this House, or any Committee thereof, this House will proceed with the utmost Severity against such Offender.-

A Motion was made, and the Question being proposed. That it is a high Infringement of the Liberties and Privileges of the Commons for any Lord of Parliament to concern himself in the Election, or for any Lord Lieutenant of any County, in that Part of the United Kingdom called Great Britain, to avail himself of any Authority derived from his Commission, to influence the Election of any Members to serve for the Commons in Parliament;

And a Debate arising in the House thereupon;

Ordered, That the Debate be adjourned till Monday Morning next.

A Motion was made, and the Question being proposed. That it is a high Infringement of the Liberties and Privileges of the Commons, for any Lord of Parliament to concern himself in the Election, or for any Governor of any County in- that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland, to avail himself of any Authority derived from his Commission to influence the Election of any Member to serve for the Commons in Parliament;

And a Debate arising in the House thereupon;

Ordered, That the Debate be adjourned till Monday Morning next.

Ordered, That the Serjeant at Arms attending this House do, from Time to Time, take into his Custody any Stranger or Strangers, that he shall see, or be informed ot to be, in the House, or Gallery, while the House, or any Committee of the whole House, is fitting; and that no Person, so taken into Custody, bedif-charged out of Custody without the special Or<J|r of the House.

Ordered, That the Back Door of the Speaker's Chamber be locked up every Morning at the Sitting of the House, and the K.ey delivered to the Clerk, to be locked up by him; and that he do not presume to deliver the same to any Person whatsoever without Order of the House; and that the Serjeant at Arms attending this House do take Care to clear the Speaker's Chamber every Day before the Door is locked up.

Ordered, That no Member of this House do presume to bring any Stranger, or Strangers, into the House, or Gallery thereof, while the House is fitting.

Ordered, That the Constables, and other Officers, of Middlesex and Westminster, do take Care, that, from Eleven of the Clock in the Morning till One in the Afternoon, and from Four till Six in the Afternoon, during the Session of Parliament, the Passages through the Streets between Temple Bar and Westminster Hall shall be kept free and open; and that no Obstructions be made, by Cars, Drays, Carts, or otherwise, to hinder the Passage of the Members to and from this House; and that the Serjeant at Arms attending this House do give Notice of this Order to the Officers aforesaid.

Ordered, That the Constables in Waiting do take Care that there be no Gaming, or other Disorders, in Westminster Hall, or the Pall'ages leading to the House, during the Sitting of Parliament; and that there be no Annoyance by Chairmen, Footmen, or otherwise, therein or thereabouts.

Ordered, That the said Orders be sent to the High Bailiff of Westminster-, and that he do lee the same put in Execution.

Ordered, That no Footman be permitted to be within the Lobby of the House, or upon the Stairs leading thereto.

Ordered, That the Serjeant at Arms attending this House do take Care that there be no Gaming, or other Disorders, in the lloom appointed for the Footmen attending the Members of this House to wait in.

Ordered, That the Serjeant at Arms attending this* House do take into his Custody such Footmen as shall presume to disobey the Orders of the House; and that no such Footmen be discharged out of Custody but by the special Order of the House.

Ordered, That to prevent the intercepting or losing of Letters directed to Members of this House, the Person appointed to bring Letters from the General Poll Office to this House, or some other Person, to be appointed by the Postmaster General, do, for the future, every Day during the Session of Parliament, Sundays excepted, conllantly attend trom Ten of the Clock in the Morning till One in the Afternoon, and for Two Hours at the kail immediately after the Kiting of the House; and also trom Five of the Clock in the Afternoon till Seven, at the Place appointed for the Delivery of the said

Letters, and take Care, during his Stay there, to deliver the same to the several Members to whom they shall be directed, or to their known Servant or Servants, or others, bringing Notes under the Hands of the Members . tending for the fame.

Ordered, That the said Officer do, upon his going away, lock up such Letters as shall remain undelivered, and that no Letter be delivered but within the Hours aforesaid.

Ordered, That the said Orders be sent to the Post-master General.

Ordered, That when any Letter or Packet, directed to this House, shall come to Mr. Speaker, he do open the fame; and acquaint the House, at their next Sitting, with the Contents thereof, if proper to be communicated to this House.

Ordered, That the Serjeant at Arms attending this House do, from Time to Time, when the House is going to Prayers, give Notice thereof to all Committees; and that all Proceedings of Committees, in a Morning, after such Notice, be declared to be null and void.

Ordered, That the Votes of this House be printed, being first perused by Mr. Speaker; and that he do appoint the Printing thereof; and that no Person, but such as he shall appoint, do presume to print the fame.

Mr. Speaker acquainted the House, That he had re- Answer of ceived from Admiral Lord Keith, the following Letter, v«c *feilh to in Return to the Thanks of this House, signified to him Thinks, by Mr. Speaker, in obedience to their Commands of the 18 th Day of May, in the last Session of Parliament.

Foudroyant, Bay of Aboukir, 15th July 1801.

Sir,

I have received your Letter of the 19th May last, transmitting to me the unanimous Vote of Thanks with which the House of Commons has been pleased to honour my Services} and those of Rear Admiral Sir Richard Bickerton, and the Captains, Officers, Seamen, and Marines, of the Fleet under my Command, who were employed in disembarking the British Troops on the Coast of Egypt, and supporting their subsequent Operations; which I have embraced the earliest Opportunity of communicating to Rear Admiral Sir Richard Bickerton, and to the Captains, Officers, Seamen, and Marines, who were employed on that Service: And I requell that you will be pleased to allure the Honour-ble House, that wejullly appreciate that distinguished Testimony bf Satisfaction with our Efforts in the Discharge of the Duty which we owe to the Public, and which our Country has always a Right to require.

I crave Permission, Sir, to express my Acknowledgements for the very obliging Terms in which you have been pleased to convey the Vote of the House to me; and to allure you of the additional Satisfaction I enjoy in having had this, honourable Testimony of public Approbation transmitted to me by one who commands my Respect and Esteem.

I have the Honour to be, with the greatest Regard,

Sir,

Your most obedient, and most humble Servant,

The Right Honourable The Speaker of the House of Commons.

Mr. IVodehouse reported from the Committee, appointed Yesterday to draw up an Address to be presented to His Majesty, That the Committee had drawn up an Address accordingly, which they had directed him to report to the House J and he read the same in his Place, and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table; Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

Most Gracious Sovereign*

We, Your Majesty's most dutiful and loyal Subjects, the Commons of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, in Parliament assembled, beg leave to return Your Majesty our most humble Thanks for Your most Gracious Speech from the Throne.

We learn, with great Satisfaction, that the Differences with the Northern Powers have been adjusted by a Convention with the Emperor of RuJ/ia, to which the Kings of Denmark and Sweden have expressed their Readiness to accede; and that Preliminaries of Peace have been ratified between Your Majesty and the French Republic.

We acknowledge Your Majesty's Goodness in having been pleated to direct Copies of these Treaties to be laid before us; and allure Your Majesty, that we shall not fail to apply our immediate Attention to the important Transactions to which they relate.

We acknowledge, with the utmost Gratitude, the Paternal Solicitude which leads Your Majesty to regret the Necessity of large additional Supplies; but, while we sincerely participate in that Sentiment, we feel the indispensible Duty of providing for the Expences which must, for a Time, be unavoidable in different Parts of the World, and of maintaining an adequate Establifti-ment on the final Restoration of Peace.

We shall be anxious for the Adoption of all such ceconomical Arrangements as may not be incontiftent with the great Object which Your Majesty has so justly at Heart, ot effectually providing for the Security of all Your Majesty's Dominions.

We a flu re Your Majesty, that we truly participate in the Gratification which Your Majesty has lo graciously been pleased to express, at the Relief which the Bounty of Divine Providence has afforded to Your People by the Abundance of the late Harvest: and we beg leave most dutifully to acknowledge Your Majesty's gracious Acceptance and Approbation of the Proofs of that Temper and Fortitude which have been manifested by all Descriptions of Your Subjects, under the various and complicated Difficulties with which they have had to contend.

We reflect, with Sentiments of just Exultation, on the distinguished Valour and eminent Services of Your Majesty's Forces by Sea and Land, which at no Period have been furpafied; and we have contemplated, with the utmost Satisfaction, the unprecedented Exertions VoL. $1.

of the Militia and Fencibles, and the Zeal and Perseverance of the Yeomanry and Volunteer Corps of Cavalry and Infantry.

We most heartily congratulate Your Majesty on the Naval and Military Operations of the last Campaign, and on the glorious and successful Ifl'ue of the Expedition to Egypt, marked, as it has been throughout, by Atchievements which, in their Consequences, and by their Example, cannot fail to conduce to the lading Advantage and Honour of this Country.

We cordially share in Your Majesty's earned Willies that Your Subjects may enjoy, in their full Extent, the returning Blefiings of Peace, in the progressive Increase of the National Commerce, Credit, and Revenues; and, above all, in the undisturbed Possession of their Religion, Laws, and Liberties, under the Safeguard and Protection of that Constitution which it has been the great Object of all our Efforts to preserv, and which it is our fixed Determination* as it is our most sacred Duty, to transmit, unimpaired, to our DescendantS;

The said Address being read a Second Time;

Resolved, Nemine Contradicente, That this House doth agree with the Committee in the said Address to be presented to His Majesty.

Resolved, That the said Address be presented to His Majesty by the whole House.

Ordered, That such Members of this House, as are of His Majesty's most Honourable Privy Council, do humbly know His Majesty's Pleasure, when He will be attended by this House.

Ordered, That His Majesty's most Gracious Speech to both Houses of Parliament be taken into Consideration Tomorrow Morning.

Resolved, Nemine Contradicente, That the Thanks of this House be given to Rear Admiral Sir James marez, Baronet, Knight of the most Honourable Order of the Bath, for his Alacrity and Zeal in pursuing, and his able and gallant Conduit in the fuccelsful Attack on the combined Squadron of the Enemy, in the Straits of Gibraltar, on the 12 th and 13 th Days of July last, by the Squadron under his Orders.

Resolved, Nemine Contradicente, That the Thanks of this House be given to the Captains and Officers of the Squadron under the Orders of the said Rear Admiral, for their gallant Conduit on that Occasion; and that the Rear Admiral be desired to signify the same to them.

Resolved, Nemine Contradicente, That this House doth highly approve of, and acknowledge, the Services of the Seamen and Marines on board the Ships under the Orders of the said Rear Admiral, in the late successful Attack on the combined Squadron of the Enemy; and that the Captains of the several Ships be desired to signify the same to their relpeilive Crews, and to thank them for their gallant Behaviour.

Ordered, That Mr. Speaker do signify the said Resolutions to Rear Admiral Sir James Saumarez.

LORD Viscount Stopford reported to the House, That His Majesty, having been waited upon (pursuant to the Order of Yesterday) humbly to know His Majesty's Pleasure, when He would be pleased to be attended by this House, had been pleased to appoint to be attended this Day, at Two of the Clock, at His Palace of Saint James.

The Order of the Day being read;

The House proceeded to take into Consideration His Majesty's most Gracious Speech to both Houses of Parliament.

And the same was again read by Mr. Speaker.

And a Motion being made, That a Supply be granted to His Majesty;

Resolved, That this House will, upon Monday Morning next, resolve itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider of that Motion.

And then the House adjourned till Monday Morning, Ten of the Clock.

Lunae, 2* die Novembris

MR. Speaker reported to the House, That the House attended His Majesty, on last, with their

Address; to which His Majesty was pleased to give this most Gracious Answer:

Gentlemen,

I thank you for this dutiful and loyal Address.

The Sentiments it conveys are fresh and satisfactory Proofs of that Attachment to My Person and Government, and of that Regard for the Honour and Interests of this Country, by which your Conduct has been invariably distinguished.

That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for effecting the Purposes aforesaid, in such Manner, and under such Regulations, as to the House shall seem meet.

A Petition of the Wardens and Commonalty of the New Bridge of Roc hefter, in the County of Kent, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Bridge across the River Medway, at Rochester, in the County of Kent, is of great public Use, but, being very narrow for Horses, Carriages, and Passengers, and the Arches thereof narrow and incommodious to the Navigation of the said River, the Petitioners have lately entered upon, and made considerable Progress in widening the Passage over the said Bridge, and also in preparing to widen one of the Arches thereof, and thereby materially to improve the Navigation of the said River, at a considerable Expence, by which a large Debt has been incurred; and that the Estates and Property belonging to the said Bridge are inadequate to discharge the said Debt, and to complete the said Works without the Assistance of Parliament; and that the Petitioners have no Power by Law to charge or mortgage the Estates belonging to the said Bridge with or for any Debt incurred in the Execution of the Works aforesaid, and it is necessary that the Petitioners should be enabled to collect a Toll on the said Bridge, and also to borrow Money on the Credit thereof, and of the Estates belonging to the said Bridge, for the Purpose of completing the said Works, and paying off the said Debt, and that further Powers should be granted: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for the Purposes above-mentioned.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the lame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Sir W Sit Edward

Most Gracious Sovereign,

We, Your Majesty's most dutiful and loyal Subjects, the Commons of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, in Parliament afi'embled, beg leave to

return Your Majesty our most humble Thanks for having been graciously pleased to lay before us, a Copy of the Preliminaries of Peace, which have been ratified by Your Majesty and the French Republic.

We allure Your Majesty, that, having taken them into our most serious Consideration, we refled, with heartfelt Gratitude, on the fresh Proof which has been afforded, on this Occasion, of Your Majesty's paternal Care for the Welfare and Happiness of Your People; and contemplate with great Satisfaction the Prospect of a Definitive Treaty of Peace, founded on Conditions, which, whilst they manifest Your Majesty's Wisdom, Moderation, and good Faith, will, we trust, be productive of Consequences highly advantageous to the iub-stantial Interests of the British Empire.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee*

That no Peer of this Realm, except such Peers of that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland as shall, for the Time being, be actually elected, and shall not have declined to serve, for any County, City, or Borough, of Great Britain, hath any Right to give his Vote in the Election of any Member to serve in Parliament.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committeey That it is a high Infringement of the Liberties and Privileges of the Commons of the United Kingdom, for any Lord of Parliament, or any Peer or Prelate of Ireland, except such as shall, for the Time being, be actually elected, and shall not have declined to serve for any County, City, or Borough, of Great Britain, to concern themselves in the Election of Members to serve for the Commons in Parliament, except only at such Elections where such Peer shall appear as a Candidate, or by himself or any others be proposed to be elected; or for any Lord Lieutenant, or Governor of any County, to avail himself of any Authority derived from his Commission to influence the Election of any Member to serve for the Commons in Parliament.

A Petition of the acting Trustees appointed in and Exeter Road* by an Act, made in the 13th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for more effectually amending several e wn* Roads leading from the City of Exeter, and for re-building or repairing Exe Bridge, and making the Avenues leading thereto more commodious, and for building a Bridge over the River Exe at or near Wear, and for amending several other Roads therein mentioned, was presented to the House* and read; Setting forth.

That the Petitioners, in pursuance of the said Act, have widened, amended, and repaired the several Roads therein mentioned, and have also re-built a Bridge over the River Exe, and made proper and convenient Avenues to the fame, as directed by the said Act; and that in carrying the Purposes of the said Act into Execution, very considerable Sums of Money have necessarily been expended, and particularly in re-building such Bridge, and making such Avenues as aforesaid, an Expence has been incurred of nearly £. 21,000; and that by Reason thereof, and of the great Extent of the said Roads, being above 160 Miles, and the increased Price of Labour, added to the Difficulty and Expence of procuring Materials in several Parts of the fame, the said Roads in general cannot be kept in such a State of Repair as the Safety and Convenience of the Traveller, and the Laws of this Kingdom, require, and in some Parts are become so ruinous that they cannot by any Means be repaired by the present Resources of the Trust; and that the Petitioners have, in pursuance of the said Act, from Time to Time taken up large Sums of Money on the Credit of the Tolls and Duties arising on the said Roads, lo that the several Sums borrowed on the Credit of the former Acts and of the said Act amount to £. 53,900; and that the several Tolls and Duties arising on the said Roads amount only to the Sum of £. 4,809 per Annum, or thereabouts, which, after paying the Sum of £. 2,156 to the Creditors for the Interest of the said Sum of £. 53,900, leaves only the Sum of £. 2,653, or thereabouts, to be applied to the Repairs of the said Roads, which the Petitioners find to be altogether insufficient for that Purpose; and that the said Act having limited the Interest of the Sums borrowed to Fourier Cent, the Petitioners have no Prospect of being able to raise any additional Sums for the Repair of the said Roads at that Rate of Interest; and that the Petitioners have caused an accurate Survey to be made of the said Roads, and, having examined able and skilful Persons respecting the State thereof, find that it will require a Sum not less than £. 12,000, to put them in good and proper Repair; and that the several Tolls and Duties already granted will be greatly inadequate to the Discharge of the Interest of the Monies now due and owing on the Credit of the said Act, or which may hereafter be borrowed for the Purposes aforesaid, and to the keeping the said Roads in good and proper Repair, and other necessary Expences attending the Execution of the said Trulls; and that it would tend greatly to further and facilitate the Execution thereof, if the Powers given by the said Act were explained, amended, and enlarged; and that the Petitioners, the Trustees nominated in the said Act for building a Bridge at Countess Wear, and for widening and repairing the Roads leading thereto, pro- cecded in the said Business, in which was expended the Sum of £.3,512. 1 or. which Money was borrowed on the Credit of the Tolls, and now remains due to the Creditors, with a considerable Sum for Interest: And

therefore

Mr. Gore Langton reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Company of Proprietors of the Somersetshire Coal Canal Navigation, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Navigation Bills, had not strictly been complied with; the Bath Chronicle, dated the ill Day of 1801, in which

Notices of the intended Application to Parliament were inserted, being produced to the Committee, a Witness was examined, who said, that, although that Paper bears Date on ‘Thursday the ill Day of , it was actually

published and circulated on Wednesday the 30th Day of 'September, it being always customary with the Publisher of that Paper to publish and circulate the same on the Day preceding that on which it bears Date; and it appearing to the Committee, that the Parish of Southfioke, through which the Line of the intended Canal is to pass, was omitted in the Notices given in the Bath Chronicle on the 17th Day of September, the Witness, being further examined, said, that the same was omitted by Mif* take, but that the Owners and Occupiers of Lands in the Parish so omitted had severally given their Consents for their Lands to be taken for the Purposes of the intended Application; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place, and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, passed in the 34th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal, with certain Railways and Stone Roads, from several Collieries in the County of Somerset, to communicate with the intended Kennet and Avon Canal, in the Parish. of Bradford in the County of Wilts-, and also, an Act, passed in the 36th Year of His said Majesty's Reign, to Vary and alter the Line of the said Canal, and to alter and amend the said Act; were severally read: — And

Mr. William Bennet, being examined, laid, That the Petitioners have made great Progress in forming the said Canal, and executing other Works belonging to or connected therewith; in the doing of which they have expended all the Money they have been able to raile by Virtue of the said Acts, and have also contracted considerable Debts, which Hill remain due and owing: That in proceeding to make and complete ac. certain Von. 57,

Part of the said Canal, called The jbunkerton Line, the Petitioners have formed a Communication between the Upper and Lower Level, by a Whimfey or Jenny Road, and did intend to have formed a limilar Communication between the Upper and Lower Level, on the stock Line of Canal, which by the said firfb recited Act, they are empowered to make, in case they should find it expedient so to do, but, it is apprehended, that such Communications will be attended with great Loss,

Delay, and Inconvenience, to the Traders on the said Canal, and to the Public; and that it would be much more convenient and a considerable Saving to the Public, if the Lines of the said Canal were completed; and finished by a Water Communication, to be formed between the Upper and Lower Levels thereof; but the Petitioners find by examining the Lands, through which they are by the said Acts authorized to make the said Canal, that they cannot make such Water Communication, without being empowered to vary and alter the Dunkerton Line of the said Canal, in the Parishes of Coombhay and Southjloke in the said County of Somerset, and the Radjlock Line, in the Parish of Wellow in the same County: — And the Witness further said.

That, in order to enable the Petitioners to discharge their present Debts and Incumbrances, and also to make the said Water Communications, and to complete the said Undertaking, it is necessary that they should be enabled to raise such further Sums of Money as may be requisite; and that the Tonnage Rates, to be taken on Goods that shall be passed from the Upper to the Lower, and from the Lower to the Upper Levels of the said Lines of Canal, should be encreased: — And the Witness added, That the Powers of the said Acts have been found insufficient and defective, and it is necessary the same should be extended, altered, explained, and amended.

Ordered, That the said Report do lie upon the Table.

MR. Gore Langton reported from the Committee,

to whom the Report was re-committed, which was made from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Company of Proprietors of the Coal

Canal Navigation, was referred; That the Committee had further examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Navigation Bills, had been complied with (except that the Parish of through which the Line of Canal is intended to pals, for about the Length of 600 Yards, was, byMiftake, omitted in the first Notices inserted in the Chronicle on the 17th Day of September; but that all the Owners and Occupiers of Lands in that Parish, through which the Line of Canal is intended to pais, had given their Con-fents for their Lands to be taken for the Purposes of the intended Undertaking); and that the Committee had thought it right to observe that the last Notices given of the said intended Undertaking were inserted in the Bath Chronicle, bearing Date the ill Day of QElober, but that it had been proved to the Committee, that, according to the established Practice of the Editor of that Paper, the same was pubJished on the Day preceding the Day of its Date, and so in fact had its Publication within the Month of September; and that the Committee had further examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the lame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table; Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz. 1

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, passed in the 34th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for making and maintaining a navigable Canal, with certain Railways and Stone Roads, from several Collieries, in the County of to communicate

with the intended Kernel and Canal, in the Parish of Bradford, in the County of and also, an Act, passed in the 36th Year of His said Majesty's Reign, to vary and alter the Line of the said Canal, and to alter and amend the said Act; were severally read: And,

Mr. William Bennet being examined, said. That the

Petitioners have made great Progress in forming the said Canal, and executing other Works belonging to or connected therewith; in the doing of which they have expended all the Money they have been able to raise by virtue of the said Acts, and have also confradted con-lidurable Debts which still remain due, and owing. — That, in proceeding to make and complete a certain Part of the said Canal, called The Line, the Peti-

tioners have formed a Communication between the Upper and Lower Level by a Whimfey or Jenny Road, and did intend to have formed a similar Communication between the Upper and Ixiwer Level on the Line of Canal, which by the said first recited Act, they are empowered to make in case they should find it expedient so to do: But it is apprehended that such Communications will be attended with great Lois, Delay, and Inconvenience to the Traders on the said Canal, and to the Public; and that it would be much more convenient, and a contiderable Saving to the Public, if the Lines of the said Canal, were completed and finished by Voi., 57.

a Water Communication to be formed between the Lower and Upper Levels thereof; but the Petitioners find by examining the Lands through which they are by the said Acts authorized to make the said Canal, that they cannot make such Water Communication without being empowered to vary and alter the DunkertonLine of the said Canal, in the Parishes of and

Jioke, in the said County of Somerset, and the Line, in the Parish of Wellow, in the same County. — And, the Witness further said. That in order to enable the Petitioners to discharge their present Debts and Incumbrances, and also to make the said Water Communications, and to complete the said Undertaking, it is necessary that they should be enabled to raise such further Sums of Money as may be requisite, and that the Tonnage Rates to be taken on Goods that shall be passed from the Upper to the Lower, and from the Lower to the Upper Levels of the said Lines of Canal, should be encrealed. — And, the Witness added, That the Powers of the said Acts have been found insufficient and defective, and it is necessary the same should be extended, altered, explained, and amended.

Ordered That the said Report do lie upon the Table.

Mr. Mainwaring reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Trustees appointed to put in Execution an Act, made in the 22d Year of the Reign

of his late Majesty, for the better repairing the Highways, and cleansing the Streets, within the'Parish of Saint Leonard, Shoreditch, in the County of Middlesex, and for better enlightening the open Places, Streets, Lanes, Passages, and Courts, there, and regulating the nightly Watch, and Beadles, within the said Parish, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Paving Bills, had- not been complied with; but that Notice of the intended Application for the Purposes mentioned in the Petition was given on the Door of the Sessions House for the County of Middlesex at the Time of the last Michaelmas Quarter Sessions, and that Notice was also given in the Paper called The Oracle and Daily Jdvertifer of the 19th, 20th, and 21st of last,

and also in The Morning Herald of the 23d, 26th, and 28th of October last, the Trustees not having come to any Determination to apply to Parliament for the Purposes mentioned in the Petition until the 8th of October last, and apprehending that the said Orders did not extend to such Applications, it being only to enlarge and amend the Powers of the former Act; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition ;'and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followethviz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, the said Act was read: And,

Robert Davies, Esquire, being examined, said. That the said Act is found in many Respects defective, and inadequate to the Purposes thereby intended: — And being further examined, he said. That since the passing of the Act, several new Streets and other Improvements have been made, which has occasioned an Increase of at least 1,500 Houses and other Buildings; and that it will be a great Convenience to the Inhabitants of the said Parish, and to all Persons resorting thereto, if Powers were given to pave and keep in repair all such of the said several Streets, Highways, and Foot Paths within the said Parish, as are not included in any other Paving or Turnpike Act, and to remove Nuisances, Obstructions, and Annoyances therein: — And the Witness added. That it will be necessary for those Purposes to have a Power to increase the Rate raised by virtue of the former Act. — Then,

Thomas Taylor, Esquire, being examined, confirmed the above Evidence.

A PETITION of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, beiqg the Owners and Proprietors of, or Persons interested in, the Open and Common Fields, Common Pastures, Common Meadows, and other Commonable Lands and Grounds, within the Manor, Parish, and Liberties, of in the County of Northampton, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the said Lands and Grounds lie inconveniently intermixed and dispersed in small Parcels, and, in their present Situation, are incapable of any considerable Improvement, and it would be very advantageous to the several Persons entitled thereto, if the same were divided and inclosed, and specific Parts and Shares thereof allotted to the Persons interested therein: And therefore praying. That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for dividing and inclosing the said Lands and Grounds, upon such Terms, and in such Manner and Form, as to the House shall seem meet.

Mr. John Smyth accordingly reported from the said Committee, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That no Peer of this Realm, except such Peers of that Part of the United Kingdom called Ireland as shall, for the Time being, be actually elected, and shall not have declined to serve, for any County, City, or Borough of Great Britain, hath any Right to give his Vote in the Election of any Member to serve in Parliament.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That it is a high Infringement of the Liberties and Privileges of the Commons of the United Kingdom, for any Lord of Parliament, or other Peer or Prdate, not being a Peer of Ireland at the Time elected, and' not having declined to serve for any County, City, or Borough of Great Britain, to concern himself in the Election of Members to lerve for the Commons in Parliament, except only any Peer of Ireland at such Eiedtions in Great Britain respectively, where such Peer shall appear as a Candidate, or by himself or any other! be proposed to be elected; or for any Lord Lieutenant cr Governor of any County, to avail himself of any Authority derived from his Commission, to ififluence the Election of any Member to serve for the Commons in Parliament.

Ordered, That the said Report be taken into further Consideration upon this Day Sevennight.

A Petition of the Mayor and Citizens of the City of Petition of Rochester, in the County of Kent, on Behalf of them- of Rochef selves and the several other Persons, whose Names are ter, nrsinft thereunder written, Inhabitants of the said City and Rochester Neighbourhood, was presented to the House, and read; BrKlseB> Taking Notice of the Bill to enable the Wardens and Commonalty of the new Bridge of Rochester, in the County of Kent, to complete the Improvements and Repairs of the said Bridge, and to raise Money for that Purpose; and setting forth. That, by the Improvements and Repairs proposed to be done by the said Bill, not only the Passage over the said Bridge will be rendered more commodious, but the Navigation of the said River be very considerably improved by the widening of one of the Arches; and that it is proposed to take a Toll for all Cattle and Carriages passing over the said Bridge; and the Petitioners conceive, that, as all Persons navigating the said River, and passing under the said Bridge, will be materially benefited by the Alterations proposed to be made in the said Arches, it is reasonable that they also Ihiould contribute towards the Expence, by which Means the Tolls to be taken for passing over the said Bridge need not be set so high; and that by the said Bill the Toll may be taken at a Turnpike Gate already erected at some Distance from the said Bridge* near the Angel Inn, in Strood, whereby Carriages and Cattle going only to Wharfs on the said River, and not passing over the said Bridge, will be liable to Toll; and the said Bill also contains other Provisions and Regulations which will be injurious to the Petitioners: And therefore praying, That they may be heard, by themselves, or Counsel, against such Parts of the Bill as may affect them, and that the same may not pals into a Law as it now Hands, or that the Petitioners may have such Relief in the Premises as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee, to whom the said Bill is committed; and that the Petitioners be heard, by themselves or Counsel, before the said Committee, upon their Petition, if they think fit.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the said Committee, That they do admit Counsel to be heard, at the same Time, in Favour of the said Bill, against the said Petition.

Ordered, That all have Vo:ces who come to the Committee, to whom the said Bill is committed.

A Petition of the several Persons, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, being Commissioners for executing Two Acts, passed for paving, cleansing, lighting, and otherwise improving, the Town of Maidstone, in the County of Kent, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That an Act was passed in the 31st Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for widening, improving, regulating, paving, cleansing, and lighting, the Streets, Lanes, and other public Passages, and Places, within the King's Town of Maidstone, in the County of Kent, for removing and preventing Encroachments, Obllrudlions, Nuisances, and Annoyances, therein, for better supplying the said Town with Water, and for repairing the Highways within the Parish of Maidstone; and that, by the said Act, the Commissioners appointed to put the same in Execution are authorized to borrow, on the Credit of the Rates thereby granted, a Sum not exceeding £.7,000, for the more expeditious Performance of the several intended Improvements; and that the Commissioners have proceeded to execute the said Act, and have made great Progress therein, for which Purpose they have borrowed and expended the Whole of the said Sum of £. 7,000, and have allb incurred several considerable Debts, which they have no Means of discharging, nor are they able to carry the Purposes of the said Act into complete Effect without further Powers; and that an Act was passed, in the 36th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for enabling the said Commissioners to raise a further Sum of Money for completing the Purposes of the said former Act; and that the Commissioners have endeavoured to Vo l. 57.

petition from a PETITION of the Mayor and Burgesses of the upon Hull, to ajL Town or Borough of Kingston-upon-Hull, in Com-prohibit the mon Council assembled, was presented to the House, and wad; Setting forth. A Petition of the Manufacturers, licensed retail Petition from Dealers, and other Inhabitants of the Borough of r£w

was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, tie* on Good*

That imported into Ireland*

That the Petitioners labour under a vety grievous Law exilling in Ireland, subjecting the Petitioners, who are not rated Merchants, to pay Six per Cent, additional Duty upon the Duties of all Goods they import (except Sugars, and a Part of Goods the Growth, Produce* and Manufacture of Great Britain); which is a complete Prohibition on Goods paying high Duties, and in all Cases highly injurious to the Petitioners, as tending to the Discouragement of Industry, Manufactures, and Enter-prize, as well as to that free Spirit of Commerce which they have a Right to enjoy by the Union, under a free and happy Constitut ion; and that the Law, of which they complain, by subjecting Manufacturers and others, who contribute so largely to the Exigencies of the State, by paying great Sums in both Licence and Excise, is highly impolitic, and creates an improper Distinction between the Subjects of II is Majesty's United Kingdom, as no such Law exists in Great Britain, where such a Tax would be more productive: And therefore praying the House will take their Cate into serious Consideration, and grant them Relief, by putting them on a Footing with the British Subjects.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

That an' Act was passed in the 2d Year of the Reign of I lis present Majesty, for the better supplying the Cities of London and Westminster with Fish, and to reduce the present exorbitant Prices thereof, and encourage Fishermen; and that, at the Time of passing the said Act, the Quantity of White Fish and Fresh Salmon brought to Billingsgate Market was very lmail in Companion with the Quantity that is now brought and Ibid there, owing to the great Increase in the Number and Size of the Fishing* Vefibls employed in the Fishery, and the present Method ot bringing fresh Salmon to Market in Ice, a Mode not vAcd until within these few Years, by which Means the Price ot Fish is greatly reduced, and the Public more amply supplied therewith; and that, from the great In-crcalc in the Quantity of Fish of all Kinds brought to Billingsgate Market for Sale, and particularly of those above lpccified, the Salesmen and Factors are unable to dispose of the same in the Manner, and according to the Regulations and Provisions, of the said Act, particularly the Articles of Fresh Salmon, Cod, Skait, and Turbot, whereby the Salt (men and Factors have frequently and unavoidably been iubjecled to Prosecutions for recovering of the Penalties instifted by the said Act; and that the Powers and Provisions of the said Act have been found, in other Respects, inconvenient and prejudicial to the Persons concerned and employed in supplying the said Market with Fish, and detrimental to the Public; and it would tend greatly to encourage and facilitate the Sale of: Fish in the said Market it the said Act was to be repealed, and if the Petitioners were inverted with such powers and Authorities, for regulating the Sale of Fish by Wholesale in the said Market, as may be deemed requisite and necessary: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for repealing the said Act, and for the better Regulation of the Sale of Fish by Wholesale in the said Market of Billingsgate, in such Manner, and under such Rules and Orders, as to the House shall seem meet.

And the said Petition was read; Setting forth, That the late Harvest has been most abundant throughout the

t t O

Realm, but the Price ot Bread is still very high; and that the Poor have, from an Idea of Scarcity, borne their Distress during the lart Two Winters with the greatest Patience, but, in the Mid ft of Abundance, it would be cruel to suffer our Fellow Creatures to be reduced to the Want of what Providence hath so amply bellowed; and that Efforts have been made to ascertain the Stock of Grain in the Country, and, through the Medium of the Clergy, Means have been used to ascertain the Number of Acres sown in the present Year with each Sort o(

Grain, in order to form tome Calculation of what further Provision might be necessary for the Consumption of the People; but, instead of answering this plain and unexceptionable Quest ion, a great Proportion of Ihe Farmers

have

have made no Return whatever, and many of the Returns which have been made are fallacious and unsatisfacftory; and that, under these Circumstances, the Petitioners are induced to think it would be expedient that Legislative Means should now be adopted for the Purpose ot obtaining the necfcflary* Information, in order to the Adoption of Measures which the present Emergency may appear to require/ and to enable Government, in Years of Scarcity, to procure a sufficient Supply of Grain at a reasonable Rate, by availing themselves of the Supply to be derived from Foreign Markets before it could be known Abroad how far the Crop in this Country wa§ likely to be deficient: And therefore praying the House will take the Premises into their Consideration, and grant such Relief therein as to them shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Petition from A Petition of the Merchants of was presented

r ' Du to ^1C House, and read; Setting forth. That the Peti-riei on Gootls tioners consider, and feel as a serious Grievance, a Law Ireland'' *nt° CX'^"‘S 'n Ireland, w'herehy all Importers of Goods, rf ' who tell lets than an original Package, are subjected to Six per Cent, on their entire Duties, whilst others, many of whom do not import more than they, are exempt from it; and that the Reaions urged in Favour of the Law at the Time it was enabled have since ceased, and the great though necessary Increase of Duty on Teas, Spirits, Wines, and many other Articles, makes this Restriction operate now almost as a Prohibition of Importation to a great Number of the Petitioners who have been bred to that Course of Business, and even the happy Restoration of Peace will, by lowering the Foreign Coli of Goods, tend to augment the Grievance; and that this Law creates an improper Distinction, has afforded llrong Temptation for Evasion or fictitious Qualifications, is frequently inconvenient to the real wholesale Merchant, and is, in every Point of View, not only partial and unjult in its Principle, but in its Operation inconfillent with, ‘and injurious to, a free Spirit of Commerce, therefore unknown in Great Britain, by their Union with which the Petitioners now hope to enjoy a like Degree of Commercial Immunities: And therefore praying the House to take the Matter into their serious Consideration, and cause this Law to be repealed, whereby every Description of Importers in Ireland will be placed on the same Footing.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

MR. Speaker acquainted the House, That he had received, from Rear Admiral Sir James Saumarez, Baronet, Knight of the Moll honourable Order of the Bath, the following Letter, in Return to the Thanks of this House, signified to him by Mr. Speaker, in obedience to their Commands of the 30th Day of last:

Sir,

His Majesty's Ship C Gibraltar Bay,

6 th January 1802.

I have received the Honour of your Letter, transmitting to me the Votes of the Honourable House of Commons on the luccefsful Attack made by the Squadron under my Orders on the combined Forces of the Enetny, in the Straits of Gibraltar, on the 12th and 13th July last.

It has been my peculiar Fortune to be honoured with the Thanks of Parliament on Four different Occasions, when Commander of a Line of Battle Ship in general Actions; but this very distinguished Mark of Approbation cannot fail to be more particularly gratifying to my Feelings when entrusted with the Command of His Majesty's Squadron; and I want Words to convey, in a more adequate Manner, my grateful Acknowledgments for the Notice with which the Honourable House have been pleased to honour my Services.

I shall take the earliest Opportunity to convey to the Captains, Officers, Seamen, and Marines, serving under my Orders, the Resolutions of the House; and I beg Leave, Sir, to return my most sincere Thanks for the hand tome and obl iging Terms in which you have been pleased to express yourself in signifying to me the Thanks of the Honourable House.

I have the Honour to be,

With Sentiments of the highest Helped and Regard,

Sir,

Your obliged and most obedient,

humble Servant,

The Right Honourable James Saumarez,

Sir John Mitford, Knight,

&c.tec. &c.

THE House beiing met, the Clerk at the Table Mr. Speaker acquainted the House, That he had, this Morn- re,5sns* ing, received a Letter from Mr. Speaker: Which he read to the House; and is as followeth; viz.

Palace Yard,

9th February 1802.

Sir,

His Majesty having been graciously pleased to signify His Intention of appointing me Chancellor of , it has become my Duty to resign the Chair of the House of Commons; which I request you to communicate to the House, at their Meeting this Day.

I must entreat you at the same Time to express to them, in the strongest Terms, the regret with which I quit the high Situation to which their Favour hadraised me; and my Gratitude for their constant and kind Assistance and Support, in my humble Attempts to discharge the arduous Duties of that important Office.

I have the Honour to be.

With the most sincere Esteem and Regard,

Sir,

Your most humble, and obedient Servant,

John Ley, Esquire, John

See. See. &c.

After which, and before any Member spoke, the Mace was brought into the House by the Serjeant, and laid under the Table.

Then Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer acquainted the House, That His Majesty, under the Circumstances referred to in Mr. Speaker's Letter, gives Leave to this House to proceed to the Choice of a new Speaker; and that it is His Majesty's Pleasure that this House should present their Speaker on Thursday next, at Two of the Clock in the Afternoon, in the House of Peers, for His Royal Approbation.

And then Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer (addref-sing himself to the Clerk, who, Handing up, pointed to him, and then fat down) moved. That the House do now adjourn till Tomorrow Morning, Ten of the Clock.

The Clerk, by Direction of the House, put the Question for adjourning the House, till Tomorrow Morning, Ten of the Clock.

And the House accordingly adjourned till Tomorrow Morning, Ten of the Clock.

Then Charles Dun das, Esquire, was proposed by Richard BrinjleySheridan, Esquire, who was seconded by the Right honourable Lord George Henry

Cavendish; and John Courtenay, Esquire, also supported the said Motion.

House.

And after a Debate in relation to both the said Persons, the Question was put by the Clerk, That the Right honourable Charles Abbot do take the Chair of this House, as Speaker; and agreed to.

Whereupon the said Mr. Abbot was conducted to the Chair by the said Matter of the Rolls, and Mr. Baker-, where, (landing upon the upper Step of the Chair, he again addressed himself to the House, and made his respectful Acknowledgments to the House, for the high Honour conferred upon him; and allured the House that it should be his constant Endeavour to merit their good Opinion, by a diligent and impartial Discharge of his Duty.

And then he fat down in the Chair; and the Mace (which before lay under the Table) was laid, by the Serjeant, upon the Table.

And Mr. Secretary at War congratulated Mr. Speaker cleft.

Then Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer taking Notice, that His Majesty's Pleasure had been signified to the House, Yesterday, that the House should present their Speaker Tomorrow, at Two of the Clock in the Afternoon, in the House of Peers, for His Royal Approbation, moved to adjourn till Tomorrow Morning, Ten of the Clock.

Then Mr. Speaker cleft put the Question for adjourning the House until Tomorrow Morning, Ten of the Clock; which being agreed to, the House was adjourned accordingly; and Mr. Speaker elect went away, without the Mace before him.

Mr. Speaker reported, That the House, at the Desire of the Lords authorized by virtue of His Majesty's Commission afore-mentioned, had been at the House of Peers, where a Commission under the Great Seal was read, authorizing and empowering His Royal Highness the Prince of Wales, His Royal Highness the Duke of York, His Royal Highness the Duke of Clarence, His Royal Highness the Duke of Kent, His Royal Highness the Duke of Cumberland, His Royal Highness the Duke of Stissex, His Royal Highness the Duke of Cambridge, His Royal Highness the Duke of Gloucester, the Lord Arch-bishop of Canterbury, the Lord High Chancellor, and several other Lords, to declare and notify His Majesty's Royal Approbation of the Choice made by this House of him to be their Speaker; and that the Lord High Chancellor, the Lord Hobart, and the Lord named also in the said Commission, did declare and notify the same accordingly.

And then Mr. Speaker repeated his respectful Acknowledgments to the House: Alluring the House of his zealous and unremitting Devotion to their Service, his prompt Obedience to their Commands collectively, and his cordial Assistance to their Labours individually: And he intreated the Assistance of the House, in support of its own Authority, to maintain its ancient and constitutional Privileges inviolate, and to uphold the regularity of its Proceedings; never forgetting that the Forms of the House were the Safeguards of its Privileges, and that those Privileges were the Rights of the People.

Copy of His Majesty's Commission

GEORGE R.

GEORGE the Third, by the Grace of God, of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, King, Defender of the Faith. To all to whom these Presents shall come. Greeting. Whereas, We have lately, for divers difficult and pressing Affairs, concerning Us, the State and Defence of Our said United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, and the Church, ordained this Our present Parliament to begin and be held at Our City of Westminster, on the Twenty-second Day of January, in the Forty-first Year of Our Reign, on which Day Our said Parliament was begun and held, and is there now holden. And whereas We have been informed, that the Lower House of Our said Parliament have lately made Choice of our Trusty and well-beloved Councillor Charles Abbot, in the room of Our Trusty and well-beloved Councillor Sir John Mitford, to be Speaker of the said Lower House of Our said Parliament, of which Choice We are graciously pleased to approve, and to allow and confirm the fame: And forasmuch as for divers Causes and Considerations We cannot conveniently at this Time be present in Our Royal Person in Our said Parliament; Know ye, That We, trusting in the Fidelity and Care of Our most dear and entirely beloved Son and most faithful Councillor George Prince of Wales, Our most dear Sons and faithful Councillors Frederick Duke of York, William Duke of Clarence, Edward Duke of Kent, Ernest Duke of Cumberland, Augujhts Duke of Sussex, Adolphus Duke of Cambridge, Our most dear Brother arid faithful Councillor William Duke of Gloucester, the most Reverend Father in God and Our faithful Councillor John Archbishop of

In Witness whereof We have cauled these Our Letters to be made Patent. Writness Ourself at Westminster, the Tenth Day of February, in the Forty-second Year of Our Reign.

and maintaining certain Collateral Cuts from the said Canal, certain Persons were united into one Body Corporate, by the Name and Style of The Company of Proprietors of the Ellefinere Canal, and were authorized and empowered to make, complete, and maintain, a Canal navigable and palfable for Boats, Barges, and other Vessels, from and out of the River Severn, within the Liberties of the Town of in the County of Salop, to unite with the River Mersey, at or near ATether pod, in the County of Chester; and also to make, complete, and maintain, several Collateral Navigable

Cuts to branch from and out of the said Canal, as in the said Act mentioned; and the said Company of Proprietors were, by the said Act, authorized to raise and contribute amongil themselves, in such Proportion a* they should think proper, a competent Sum of Money for making and completing the said Canal, Collateral Cuts, and the llefervoirs, Feeders, Ways, Quays, Wharfs, and other Works and Conveniencies belonging or requisite thereto, not exceeding the Sum of £.400,000, except as therein is mentioned; and, if the said Sum should be found insufficient for making and completing the said intended Canal and Collateral Cuts, and the other Works by the said Act authorized to be made, and all necessary Charges and Expences relating thereto, the said Company of Proprietors were, by the said Act, enabled to raile and contribute amongst themselves, in the Manner in the said Act mentioned, any ‘further or other Sum of Money, for completing and perfecting the said Undertaking, not exceeding the Sum of £.50,000; and, in case the said Company of Proprietors should be desirous of raising the said Sum of£.50,000, or any Part thereof, or any further Sum of Sums of Money, not exceeding, in the Whole, the Sum of £.50,000, in addition to the said several Sums of £. 400,000 and £. 50,000, by Mortgage of the said Undertaking, they were by the said Act authorized to borrow, and take up at Interest, all or any Part of the said several Sums of £. 50,000 and £. 50,000, on the Credit of the said Navigation and Undertaking, in Manner in the said Act mentioned; and that the said Company of Proprietors were by the said Act authorized to take and receive, for the Use and Benefit of the said Company, the several Rates therein mentioned, for the Tonnage and Wrharfage of all Coals, Stone, Timber, Merchandize, and other Goods, Matters, and Things whatsoever, which should be carried or conveyed upon any Part of the said Canal and Collateral Cuts, or any of them; and it was thereby enacted, That none of the said Rates should be payable, demanded, or taken, by virtue of the said Act, for, or in respect of, any Boat, Barge, or Other Vessel, laden with Coal, Coak, Culm, Lime, or Lime Stone only, which might pass, or be navigated along any Part of the said Canal between Pont Cyfyltee and the upper End of the Cegedog Valley,

near Brumbo, in the County of Denbigh, provided such Boat, Barge, or other Veil'd, should pass or be navigated with the same Lading, Ten Miles at the lead along any other Part of the said Canal and Collateral Cuts, or any of them, and should pay Tonnage, after the Rates in the said Act mentioned, for such Ten Miles, at the lead, in respect of the same Boat, Barge, or other Veil'd, and the Lading therein; and that, by several subsequent Acts, passed in the 36th and 4ill Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, the said Company of Proprietors were authorized and empowered to vary the Line of the said Canal and Cuts in the said Act mentioned, and to make, extend, and maintain, several new Branches, to communicate therewith; and the Powers given by the said Act of the 33d Year of the Reign of His present Majesty were, by the said respective Acts of the 36th and 41st Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, extended, varied, enlarged, and amended; and that the making and maintaining of that Part of the said Canal between Pont Cyfyltee and the upper End of the Cegedog Valley, will be attended with a very considerable Expence; and it is reasonable that the said Company of Proprietors should, if they make and maintain the fame, be authorized to have, receive, and take, the like Rates of Tonnage and Wharfage upon and on the Banks thereof, as they are by the said Act of the 33d Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, authorized to take and receive, in respect of Coals, Coak, Culm, Stone, Lime, Lime Stone, Timber, Merchandize, and other Goods, Matters, and Things, which shall be carried and conveyed upon any other Part of the said Canal and the Collateral Cuts
