A Petition of the Ship Owners of the Port of . Petition of

land near the Sea, in the County Palatine of , of su^iedaud

was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice against of the Bill for improving the Tinmouth Lighthouse Li^hthouse and Light, and for authorizing additional Light Duties Bill, in respect of such Improvement; and Setting forth,

That the Tolls or Dues now received by the Person seised of the said Lighthouse, have, in consequence of the great Increase in the Number of Ships at the Ports of Newcastle and Sunderland, been augmented in a very

large Proportion, and that any Advance upon them is unreasonable and unnecessary for the Purposes for which such Tolls were originally granted and made payable; and that Tinmouth Lighthouse is built on the Main Land, at the Distance of Seven Miles North of Sunderland Harbour, and therefore Ships trading from that Harbour to any of the Southern Ports are seldom in Sight of, and are rarely, if ever, materially benefited thereby; and that the Ships on their light Passage from their Port of Delivery to the Southward of the Port of Sunderland, are occasionally benefited by Tinmouth Light; but the Dues already paid, viz. One Shilling Ship each and every Voyage, are much more than adequate to any Advantage that can be derived from such intended Improvement of the said Lighthouse or Light:

And therefore praying, That the House will take the Premises into Consideration, and that the Coals, and other Goods and Merchandize, exported from the said Port of Sunderland to the Ports lying to the Southward of the same Port, and the Ships employed in that Branch of the Trade, and the Cargoes thereof, may be exempt from the Duties to be imposed in and by the said Bill.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table, until the said Bill be read a Second Time.

Mr. O'Hara reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Merchants, Traders, and other Inhabitants of the Town of Slin the County of Sligo, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Paving Bills, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter, of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, made in the Parliament of Ireland in the 40th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled,

" An Act for paving, cleansing, lighting, and improving, the Streets, Quays, Lanes, and Passages, in the Town of Sligo, in the County of Sligo; for establishing a Nightly Watch in said Town; for supplying the said Town with Pipe Water, and for improving and regulating the Port and Harbour thereof," was read: — Then,

Mr. Thomas Griffith being examined, said. That the said Act is highly injurious in its Provisions to the several Inhabitants of the said Town of Sligo, inafrhuch as a Power is given to the Corporation, created by the said Act, of imposing such Taxes on the several Lands and Houses of the Petitioners, situate in the said Town, and the Precincts thereof, as to them shall seem proper, to the Amount of about £. 18 per Cent, on the Annual Value of all the Property within the said Town, and Precincts thereof, and a very considerable Tax on the Tonnage of the Shipping trading to the said Port is also Vested in the said Corporation; and the said Act also empowers the said Corporation to raise, on the Credit of the said Taxes, the Sum of £.6,000, without requiring any Account to be made of the Application of the several Sums of Money by them received by such Taxes, or of the said Sum of £.6,000; nor is the Misapplication thereof, in any rel'pest, prevented or con-trouled by the said Act; That a Power is also given to the said Corporation of appointing Officers to carry the said Act into Execution, with such Salaries, to be paid out of the said Taxes, as the Corporation may from Time to Time think fit to appoint; and the said Act not only permits the Members of the said Corporation to be eligible to such Offices, but omits to prescribe any Limitation to the Amount of their Salaries, and the Officers so to be appointed are only removeable from their respective Offices at the mere Will of the said Corporation who appoints them; that the said Corporation is also empowered to enter into Contracts for the Execution of the Works authorized to be made, erected, and maintained, by the said Act, and the Execution of such Contrafts are to be paid out of the said Taxes; but no Provision is niade so prevent the Members of the said Corporation from becoming the Contractors with the Corporation, and undertaking the making, erecting, and maintaining', such Works, and for the due Performance of such Contrafts, by which they the Contractors would be only accountable to themselves: That a Power is also given by the said Act to the Provost of the said Town for the Time being, or any justice of the Peace for the County of Sligo (being a Member of the said Corporation) to convict on the View, or by the Oath of One or more Witness or Witnesses, Persons offending against the said Act, on whom Fines are thereby imposed, and to levy such Fines by Distress and Sale, and to imprison Persons in default of Payment of such Fines; and no Appeal whatever is given by the Act from such Conviction (except in one Instance only) by which the said Corporation are both Judges and Accusers in their own Cause; nor are the Fines, when levied, applicable to the Purposes of the Act:; and although such Fines may amount to a very considerable Sum annually, they are, by the said Act, to be paid to the Person whom the Provost may employ to levy the same, and the Person who shall convict the Offender on whom the Fine has been imposed, according to the Discretion of the Provost. — And the Witness further laid. That the said Act is so framed, that the Powers thereby given are, in effect, vested in the Burgesses of the Borough of Sligo alone, as the Burgesses for the Time being of the said Borough are to be Members of the Corporation so created; and although the said Act names and constitutes Twelve other Persons Members of the said Corporation, yet several of the Persons so nominated never did reside in Ireland, and others of them have not resided in the County of Sligo for many Years; and that by the said Act, any Seven or more of the said Corporation are empowered to nominate such Persons as they think fit in the Place of the Members of the said Corporation who declined to act, and thus the Burgesses of the said Borough, having in effect the Nomination of the other Members of the said Corporation slave Two Persons) they virtually possess the Powers given by the said Act; that the said Burgesses are Twelve in Number, Three only of whom reside in the said Town, and others of them are Strangers to the said Town and its Interests, and the Petitioners have' not any Share whatever in the Election of the said Burgesses, nor can they in any Manner controul the Nomination of the Persons who shall succeed to the Office of Burgesses of the said Borough; that the Powers so given are the more liable to Abuse, as the future Members of the said Corporation may be elected without regard either to Residence in the said Town or County of Sligo, or any Qualification whatsoever specified by the Act. — And the Witness added. That no Part whatever of the aforesaid Sum of £.6,000 has been borrowed under the said Act, nor has any Tax whatever been as yet levied of the Properties of the Petitioners by the Authority thereof, and therefore no Injury can be done to any Individual by the Repeal thereof by his having lent Money on the Credit thereof.

Ordered, That the said Report be re-committed.

Ordered, That the said Report be re-committed to the Committee to whom the said Petition was referred.

Petition of Coroners for Augmentation of Fees, reported.

A2 Geo. III. 15 0 Mar H233

passed in the 25th Year of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the Second, for giving a proper Reward to Coroners for the due Execution of their Office, and for the Amoval of Coroners, upon a lawful Conviction, for certain Misdemeanors, was read: — And,

Mr. George Hodgson Junior, being examined, said, That the Fee of Twenty Shillings for taking each Inquisition, and Nine Pence a Mile from their own Houses only for travelling Expences, as settled by the said Act (being upwards of Fifty Years ago) are, on Account of the Decrease of the Value of Money, and the advanced Price of every Necessary of Life, as well as the Charges for travelling, very inadequate to the Expences which Coroners are subject to, in order to the punctual and faithful Observance of the Duty of their Office: That the Coroners are required, and do attend at the several Assizes, and frequently at the Quarter Sessions, for which no Fee or Recompence, Compensation for Expences, or Loss of Time, is provided by the said Act, or by any other Means whatsoever: — Then,

Mr. Charles Jemtnet being examined, said. That, in Addition to the Caufts before-mentioned, the present Duties upon Horses and Carriages of every Denomination fall heavy on those Coroners, who, on Account of their Districts being large, are obliged to keep Horses and Carriages for enabling them to execute their Offices with that Dispatch and Alacrity which is indifpcnfably necessary for the Service of the Public; and that the Coroners in general are subject to various other Expences and Inconveniences: — And,

Mr. George Hodgson, Junior, being again examined, said, That the travelling Expences far exceed the present Allowances made to the Coroner.

and maintaining such Works, and for the due Performance of such Contracts, by which they, the Contractors, would be only accountable to themselves: That a Power is also given by the said Act to the Provost of the said Town for the Time being, or any Justice of Peace for the County of Sligo (being a Member of the said Corporation) to convict on the View, or by the Oath of One or more Witness or Witnesses, Persons offending against the said Act, on whom Fines are thereby imposed, and to levy such Fines by Distress and Sale, and to imprison such Persons in default of Payment of such Fines; and no Appeal whatever is given by the Act from such Conviction (except in one Instance only) by Which the said Corporation are both Judges and Ac-cufers in their own Cause; nor are the Fines, when levied, applicable to the Purposes of the Act; and although such Fines may amount to a very considerable Sum annually, they are, by the said Act, to be paid to the Person whom the Provost may employ to levy the same, and the Person who shall convict the Offender on whom the Fine has been imposed, according to the Discretion of the Provost. — And the Witness further said, That the said Act is so framed, that the Powers thereby given are in effect vested in the Burgesses of the Borough of Sligo alone, as the Burgesses for the Time being of the said Borough are to be Members of the Corporation so created; and although the said Act names and constitutes Twelve other Persons, Members of the said Corporation, yet several of the Persons so nominated never did reside in Ireland, and others of them have not relided in the County of Sligo for many Years; and, that by the said Act, any Seven or more of the said Corporation, are empowered to nominate such Persons as they think fit, in the Place of the Members of the said Corporation who declined to act, and thus the Burgesses of the said Borough, having in Effect the Nomination of the other Members of the said Corporation save Two Persons) they virtually possess the Powers given by the said Act: That the said Burgesses are Twelve in Number, Three only of whom reside in the said Town, and others of them are Strangers to the said Town, and its Interests; and the Petitioners have not any Share whatever in the Election of the said Burgesses, nor can they in any Manner controul the Nomination of the Persons who shall succeed to the Office of Burgesses of the said Borough: That the Powers so given are the more liable to Abuse, as the future Members of the said Corporation may be elected without Regard either to Residence in the said Town or County of Sligo, or any Qualification whatsoever specified by the Act. — And the Witness added. That no Part whatever of the aforesaid Sum of £.6,000 has been borrowed under the said Act, nor has any Tax whatever been as yet levied of the Properties of the Petitioners by the Authority thereof; and therefore no Injury can be done to any Individual by the Repeal thereof, by his having lent Money on the Credit thereof.

Mr. Speaker,

The Isolds have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for raising the Sum of One Million, by Loans or Exchequer Bills, for the Service of Great Britain, for the Year One thousand Eight hundred and Two; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act to repeal the Duties on Cinnamon imported by the India Company, and on Cassia Lignea of all Sorts, and for granting new Duties in lieu thereof; and to repeal the Custom Duties on certain Hides and Skins; and to repeal certain Duties granted by an Act of the last Session of Parliament, upon Box Wood imported, and granting new Duties in lieu thereof; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill; intituled, An Act to indemnify such Persons as have omitted to qualify themselves for Offices and Employments, and to indemnify Justices of the Peace, or others, who have omitted to register or deliver in their Qualifications within the Time directed by Law, and for extending the Time limited for those Purposes until the Twenty-fifth Day of December One thousand Eight hundred and Two; to indemnify* Members and Officers in Cities, Corporations, and Borough Towns, whole Admissions have been omitted to be stamped according to Law, or, having been stamped, have been lost or mislaid, and for allowing them until the Twenty-fifth Day of December One thousand Eight hundred and Two to provide Admissions duly stamped; to permit such Persons as have omitted to make and file Affidavits of the Execution of Indentures of Clerks to Attornies and Solicitors, to make and file the same on or before the First Day of Michaelmas Term One thousand Eight hundred and Two; to allow, until the Twenty-fourth Day of December One thousand Eight hundred and Two, Persons who have omitted to pay the Duties on the Indentures and Contrafts of Clerks, Apprentices, or Servants, to make Payment of the same; to indemnify such Persons as have neglected to obtain Certificates of Admission as Solicitors or Attornies, Notaries or Proctors, and for extending the Time limited for that Purpose until Two Months after the passing of this Act; to indemnify Persons who have printed or published Pleadings and other Proceedings in Courts of Law or Equity, upon which the Name and

Yol. 57.

Place of Abode of the Printer has not bech printed; and for indemnifying Deputy Lieutenants and Officers of the Militia, who have neglected to transmit Descriptions of their Qualifications to the Clerks of the Peace within the Time directed by Law, and for extending the Time limited for that Purpose until the First Day of Septembet One thousand Eight hundred and Two; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act Falmouth and for continuing the -Term, and altering and enlarging the Powers, of Two Acts, passed in the First and Twenty-first Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, for amending and widening the Road leading from the Town of Falmouth, in the County of Cornwall, through the Towns of Penryn, Helstone, and Marazion, and from thence to and over Marazion River and Bridge, and Two hundred Feet to the West ward of the said River and Bridge; without any Amendment.

A Petition of the Lord Mayor, Aldermen, and Livery of London, in Common Hall assembled, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioners, feeling themselves much aggrieved Ly the partial and unequal Operation of the Tax upon Income, as well as the vexatious Mode by which it is carried into Exe-, cution, which, in their Judgment, militates in a most eftential Degree against the ancient and free Principles of the BriiiihConstitution, beg Leave to represent to the

House some of the intolerable Grievances under which they labour; and that the Petitioners conceive it to be an incontrovertible Principle, that 'faxes ought to be equitable, and proportionably levied, and that Property ought to be the Balls of Taxation, more especialiy when applied to Taxes raised for the Purpose of carrying on a W ar, one of the avowed Objects of which was the Preservation of Property, it appearing to than to be founded in lvcafui and Justice that Property should contribute toward: us own Support; and that, in the Opinion of the Petitioners, the said Tax is a direct Violation of this Principle, Income not appearing to them to form a just Ci.terion, either of the Properly of Individuals or of their Ability to contribute, many Persons deriving an Income from theirpersonal Exertions in their respective Trad cl and Professions, others from Annuities, &c. who may neverrhdcls pofllfs little or no permanent Property; therefore they trull the House will perceive the extreme Hard ship and Partiality of taxing Incomes anfing from such temporary, precariou, and fluctuating Sources, in the iauic Proportion as the Income proceeding from landed and uir.d'd Property; and that the said Tax has already produced the no, it lcrious and alarming Consequences, and by operating chiefly upon the Middle Chiles of the People (who can have no Resource in Retrenchment) has had an obvious Tendency to check Industry; and that the said Tax has been one great Cause of the exccfnve high Price of all the Necellaries of Life, and of the rapid and enormous Increase of the Poor Rates throughout the Kingdom, to tile great Grievance and Distress of those of 11 is Majesty's faithful Subjects, who contribute to those Rates, as well as of the many deplorable and afflicted Objects who are supported by them? and who have heretofore maintained themselves v. ith Decency and Comfort; and that great and excessive as these Evils may appear, they form but a small Part of the ( frieva.v es of wbuh the Petitioners now complain, compared with the . Manner in which the said Act is carried into Execution, whereby the tree Principles of our once-envied Constitution are violated and infringed upon, by the Etl.ihfilhmenl of an inquisitorial Power, behue whom the Petitioners arc compelled to disclose t'-c most nfinute and private Circumstances of their Trade and Families; a Circumstance hitherto unknown in this Countin', and which has never been exercised except by Creditors in Cales of Insolvency; and that this PwA.r being veiled in Commissioners, who may either be their Rivals in Trade, or with whom they may have Commercial Intercourse, subjects the Petitioners to i r,dlelis Trouble and Vexation, and may be attended wit1' the it.oft ruinous Consequences; and that the Petitioners are well allured, that under the Apprchcn-lh n of theft- Evils, many Persons in a State of Infiol-vr:.i v 1. ve b . :i induced to make a Return of Income, to ti.e g mi Injury of their Creditors, and ethers, to a

subvert the Principles of Liberty, and to depret's that independent Spirit which has ever been the Charac-teriftic of Engiijhmen, and the surest Support of National Prosperity; and for these, and various other Reasons which the Petitioners could state, no Principle of Taxation can be so revolting to their Feelings: And therefore praying, That the House, taking these Matters into their ierious Confederation, will grant the Petitioners Relief, by an immediate Repeal of the said Tax.

City of London, produced to the Committee an Account, containing a brief Statement of the Receipts and Payments in respect of the £.72,000 granted by Parliament as aforesaid; by which Account it appeared, that the Receipts on account of the Undertaking amounted to the Sum of£.72,341. 6 s. 2d.; ancj that the Charges and Expences attending the same (including the Sum of £.24,183. 16s. 3 d.paid for the Purchase of Part of the Land and Buildings necessary for that Purpose) amounted to the Sum of £.69,185. 15J. leaving a Balance of £.3,156. ior. — And,

Mr. James Montague, of the Surveyor's Office, Guildhall, Rated, That the Value of the l-and and Buildings remaining to be purchased to complete the Undertaking had been ascertained by Juries, and amounted to the Sum of £.10,604. — And he further Rated, That there Rill remainsdue and unpaid, for Work done at and on account of the said Canal, and not included in the before-mentioned Statements, the Sum of £. 11,004: — And,

Mr. Croivther further Rated, That he had calculated

the Expence of redeeming the Land Tax on the ERates purchased, and to be purchased, for the Purposes of the Canal, at the Sum of £. 1,000; and that the said Four Sums of £. 10,604, £.11,004, £.41,950, and £.1,000, making together £.64,558,' were necessary for completing the Undertaking; but inasmuch as the Balance in Favour of the Fund, as before Rated, amounted to £.3,156. ior. id. and the Balance due from the West India Dock Company, for Lands, &c. purchased under the Directions of the Act of Parliament for their Use, including sundry Payments of Rent, Taxes, &c. in respect of such laR-mentioned Lands, &c. amounted to £.6,874. 155. 6 d.;and the Proportion to be paid by the West India Dock Company of the Expences of obtaining the Act, as well as attendant on the Purchases made in pursuance thereof for their Use, would reduce the Sum necessary to be advanced for completing this important Undertaking to the Sum of £.50,000: — -And, Mr. JeJJ'of also Rated, That the principal Cause of the Sum of £.72,000 proving inadequate, aroie from a Clause in the Act of Parliament, compelling the Purchase of the Whole cf each Proprietor's Land and Premises, Part of which only was wanted for the Purposes of the Act, whereby a large Quantity of Land, and valuable Buildings, more than the Undertaking required, had been of Necessity purchased; and that a considerable additional Expence had been occasioned in consequence of Compensation being made to Parties inte-reRed in the ERates, for Good Will, &c. as directed by the Act, for which no Calculation had been made in the ERimate; and that the Value of the Land, &c. which was originally eRimated at £. 13,000, had, by the Means aforesaid, been increased to £.34,787. — He

Taking Notice of the Bill for repealing an Act, passed in the 21st Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for repairing the Road leading from the Stones -End, in Kent Street, in the Parish of Saint George, Southwark, to Dartford, and other Roads therein mentioned, in the Counties of Kent and Surrey, and for more effectually repairing and improving the said Roads; and for lighting and watching, or guarding a certain Part thereof; and also for increasing the Compensations which, by virtue of Two Acts, passed in the 26th and 27th Years of the Reign of his late Majesty, are payable, in lieu of Statute Duty, by the Parishes of East Greenwich and Saint Pau!y Deptford, to the Treasurer of the said Roads; and also for exonerating the Trustees of the said Roads from the Repair and Management of so much of the Branch Road, leading from the Stones End in Bermondsey Street to the Turnpike Gate at or near Saint Thomas-a-Waterings, in the County of Surrey, as lies within the Parish of Saint Mary Magdaleny Bermondsey, and placing the same under the Repair and Management of the Trustees for putting in Execution another Act, passed in the 38th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for repairing the Road or Street from Free School Street, Southwark, to Dockhead, and other Roads therein described; and Setting forth, That this is a Part of the Great Line of Road leading from Dover to the Capital of the Kingdom; that Foreigners from all Parts of Europe, and Travellers of every Description, as well as the Petitioners, contribute to its Maintenance; and that it more immediately communicates with the populous Towns and Villages of Deptford, Greenwich, Woolwich, Lewifham, and Eltham, and Two of His Majesty's Dock Yards, and Ordnance Warren, the Safety, Convenience, and Accommodation of whose Inhabitants, as well as the numerous Persons connected with the Public Service, ought to be attended to; but the Petitioners have, with Concern, observed the frequent Robberies and dreadful Accidents on this Road, and that, whilst almost every other Road in the Neighbourhood of London is watched, lighted, and watered, this great Approach to the Capital of the Kingdom from the Continent has been, in these Respects, totally neglected; and that the watching, lighting, and watering certain Parts of the said Road, more particularly from East Greenwich to Saint Thomas-ad Caterings, and guarding

ing the Road leading over Black heath and Shooter's Hill to Welling, and making the same more safe, is therefore a public Concern, would be highly beneficial to the Public, as well as creditable and ornamental to the Capital of the Kingdom; And therefore praying, That Provision may be made in the said Bill, and positive Directions given for effectually watching, lighting, watering, and guarding so much of the said Road; or that the House will do otherwise in the Premises, as to them shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

A Petition of the Incorporated Society , in Dublin, Petition for for promoting English Protestant Schools in Ireland, being offered to be presented to the House; testantScbook

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer (by His Majesty's 111 *"" Command) acquainted the House, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read j Setting forth. That the Charter Schools of Ireland have, from their original Institution, been uniformly recommended from the Throne by the Lord Lieutenants of Ireland for the Time being, to that Consideration from Parliament which the Interests of Religion, and the good Education of Youth, peculiarly demand, and they are happy to find that the Institution Was deemed worthy of a Continuance of the like Support from this House in the last Session of Parliament; and that the unsettled and precarious State of Public Affairs in Ireland, and the great Increase of Expence required for the Maintenance of the Children. during. the last Four Years, precluded the Petitioners from* keeping their Schools in their general State of Repair, in consequence of which several of them are at present in such a Condition as will require the Expenditure of a considerable Sum to render them fit for the convenient Accommodation of the Children; and that the Number of Children in their Schools and Nurseries at Michaelmas last, by the Returns made to the Society, was 1,^70, of whom the greater Part (now cloathed, maintained, and educated m the

Principles of pure Christianity) must be dismissed to Penury, Ignorance, and Profligacy, without such Parliamentary Aid as shall appear to be necessary: And therefore praying the House, to take their present State into Consideration, and grant the Petitioners such Aid aa will enable them to support their several Schools and Nurseries upon a Cure Footing until the next Session of Parliament.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

MR. Frere reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Governor, Deputy Governor, Assistants, and Guardians of the Poor, in the City and County of Norwich, and Liberties of the fame, was re-

ferred , That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, passed in the 10th Year of the Reign of Queen Anne, for erecting a Workhouse in the City and County of the City of Norwich, for the better Employment and maintaining the Poor there, was read: — And,

Mr. William Simpson being examined, said, That the said Governor, Deputy Governor, Assistants, and Guardians of the Poor, have proceeded in the Execution of the said Act; but that the several Powers and Provisions contained therein have been found insufficient for the several Purposes thereby intended; but, if the Powers and Provisions of the said Act were enlarged and altered, a new Workhouse might be erected, and the Poor of the said City and County might thereby be better and more comfortably maintained and supported, and at a lei's Expence than they are at present.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for altering and enlarging the Powers of an Act, made in the 10th Year of the Reign of her late Majesty Queen Anne, intituled, "An Act for erecting a Workhouse in the City and County of the City of Norwich, for the " better Employment and maintaining the Poor there," so far as the same relates to the erecting a new Work-house within the said City and County, for the better Maintenance of the Poor thereof: And that Mr. Frere and Mr. Windham do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

Lord Granville Leveson Gower reported from the Committee, appointed to consider of giving Powers to Justices of the Peace for the more effectually repairing County Bridges, and to report the fame, together with their Opinion thereupon, to the House; That the Committee had considered the Matter to them referred; and had come to several Resolutions, which they had directed him to report to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the Resolutions of the Committee were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee* That the Powers given by the different Statutes now in Force, relative to the Repair of County Bridges, are in some Respects defective.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Surveyors of County Bridges, appointed by Justices of the Peace at their General Quarter Sessions* should have the same Power to get, take, and carry away* Stones, Gravel, Sand, and other Materials, for the Repair of Roads over Bridges, and the Roads for the Space of Three hundred Feet at each of the Ends thereof, and to remove Obllrudlions and Annoyances to such Bridges and Roads, as are given to the Surveyors of Highways by virtue of an Act, passed in the 13th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, making Satisfaction for the Damages done thereby in the same Manner as is directed by the said Act-

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Justices of the Peace, in General Quarter Sessions, should be empowered to alter the Situation of County Bridges, and to wideil and enlarge the fame, and the Roads for the Space of Three hundred Feet at each of the Ends thereof, and to order their Surveyor to agree for the Recpmpence to be made for the Ground to be taken for those Purposes, not exceeding One Acre at any One such Bridge; and, if the said Surveyor cannot agree with the Owner or Owners for the Purchase thereof, or, by reason of the Absence of such Owner or Owners, shall be prevented from treating, then the said Justices shall have Power to empannel a Jury at the Quarter Sessions, to assess the Compensation for such Lands, and for the Damage to be done, in the same Manner as they are authorized and empowered by the said A<fl of the 13th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, in relation to Highways.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Powers and Provisions of the said Statute of the 13th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, relative to Highways, and the Surveyors of Highways in general, should* be extended to County Bridges, and Roads at the Ends thereof, and the Surveyors of such Bridges and Roads, as for as the same can be extended and applied.

Petition for A Petition of the Governors of the House of Industry, HouserffthC Dublin, being offered to be presented to the House, Industry in Mr. Corry (by His Majesty s Command) acquainted Dublin. the House, Toat His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, anjlread; Setting forth. That, in the nth and 12th Year of His present Majesty's Reign, an Act passed, authorizing the building an House of Industry in every County of Ireland, for the Reception of the helpless Poor thereof, and for keeping in lleftraint Sturdy Beggars and Vagabonds; and that in pursuance thereof, an House of Industry was built in the County of the City of Dublin; and that it is a fundamental Rule of this Institution, that the apparently helpless Poor should be admitted to the Relict it affords without producing any Certificate of their distressed Condition, or any Recommendation; and that it is now, therefore, become supplementary to all other Institutions for the Relief of the Indigent, by being at all Times open to those whom the Hospitals of the Kingdom, appropriated to particular Purposes, are unable to relieve from Limitation of Plan, or Defect of Revenue; and that the helpless Poor, and the Vagrant Beggar, the Infant, the Adult; the Sick, the Aged, and the Alien, the Idiot, and tire Maniac, are there admitted into separate Wards, and under Arrangements adapted to their particular Circumstances; and that this Institution restrains the vagrant, idle, and refractory, educates the Infant Poor, gives seasonable Relief in the Moment of general Calamity, leaving no Room for popular Clamour, or Pretence for disturbing public Tranquillity; and that its Regulations invite no fraudulent Claims on National Benevolence, measures out adequate Chastisement to Idleness and Vice, and obtains for the Public that Portion of Labour of which the infirm Poor are {till capable; and that the Discipline established by the Petitioners has enabled many of the Adult, but heretofore idle and vicious Poor, in consequence of the Skill and Habits of Industry acquired in the House, to support themselves Abroad, and to relieve the Public from the Burthen of their Maintenance; thus making Room for the aged Poor, and Children occupied with useful Education, which lait Class, under the Care of the Petitioners, has increased to a Degree far exceeding their present Means of Accommodation; and that, fof the Vol. 57.

259

Purpose of carrying their Plans of Improvement into complete Effect, and rendering the Institution more exteniively beneficial, the Sum of £. i ,000 Is necessary. for the Purchase of additional Ground, and the Sum of £. 2,oco towards building a Fever Hospital, additional.

Work Shops, and enlarging the Asylums for industrioui Children; and that the Infirmary attached to the House of Industry, not being sufficiently extensive for the Reception of the Number of tick Poor applying for Admission, the Petitioners received the Commands of his Excellency Marquis Cornwallis, then Lord Lieutenant, to open a Fever Hospital in Brown Street, ', until Accommodation could be prepared in the House of Industry; and that the Petitioners, have, in confer quence, opened the said Hospital for Fifty Patients on the ift of April last, from which Period it has continued full, and all Persons, iabouring under contagious Fever, are there admitted without any Recommenda^ tion: And therefore praying the House to grant such Sum for the Support of the Institution for One Year, as to them may seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the Governors of the Foundling Hospital g*,‘*l0i!J £°f in Dublin, being offered ta be presented to the House; the Foundiinf

Mr. Corry (by His Majesty's Command) acquainted Hospitalin the House, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was bfought up, and read;

Setting forth. That the Legislature having, under a late Act, thought fit to establish the Institution under the present Government, the Governors consider it their Duty to explain to the House, as concisely as pofifible, the State of this Charity, with the Advantages that have arisen from the Regulations adopted therein; and that on the 5th of November 1801 there Were supported by the Charity 3,962 Children, of whom 660 were in the Hodfe, aged Nine Years and upwards, Fourteen Infants in the Nursery, and 3,288 at Nurse in the Country, of whom 109 have been sent thither on account of their bad State of Health; and that the Children of Nine Years old and upwards are carefully instructed in Reading, Writing, Arithmetic, and the Principles of the Prcn testant Religion; and that several useful Manufactures have been established in tlje House for the Instruction and Employment of the Children; by which they have been enabled, in feme Degree, to lighten the Expence of their Maintenance and Cloathing, and have made feme Progress in acquiring useful Habits of Industry; and that, whilst the Foundling Charity is open to the indiscriminate and unlimited Admiiffion of Infants, and lo long as lb great a Difficulty exists to the apprenJ tieing or otherwise placing the grown Children out in the World, in such a Situation as shall afford a reasonable Prospect of rendering them useful and industrious Members of Society, the Charges of such an Institution cannot be estimated so precisely as might be done under the general Circumstances; but the House may be assured, that it will be the unceasing Object of the Governors to keep every Expence as low as possible, consistently with the humane Purposes of the Charity, and that if any Savings can be made, they will, as heretofore, be faithfully brought forward in Account to the Public: And therefore praying. That the House will be pleased to make such Grant as they shall think meet, to enable the Governors to support the Expences of the fcxifting Establishment, and such further Sum as they shall think proper to enable them to provide an effectual Remedy for the Difficulties under which the In-flitution now labours, and thereby more completely to fulfil the Purposes for which it was originally established.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

That they have now in the School 300 Children, and that the Maintenance of that Number, at the Rate of £.14 Sterling per Child per Annum, amounts to £.4,200 Sterling per Annum, such Estimate including an Increase at the Rate of £. 1 per Child per Annum beyond the Estimate returned last Year, partly in respect of Restitution of Salaries made to several of the Officers of the Institution, who had relinquished their Salaries during the deprefied State of the Funds, partly also in respect of the Increase of some of their Salaries in consequence of the increased Number of Children, and partly in respect to the further increased Expences which will necessarily be incurred by a Plan now in Contemplation, for instructing the Children in useful Trades; and that they have an Income only of about £.200 per Annum, arising from Legacies and Donations, which reduces the Amount for which they find themselves obliged to apply to Parliament, for the Purposes above-mentioned, to £.4,000 Sterling; and that an additional Expence will necessarily be incurred in the ensuing Year, for repairing the present Buildings, adding others thereto, and accommodating the Whole to the proposed Plan of Improvement for instructing the Children in useful Trades; which last Head of Expences is estimated at £.50o Sterling; the Petitioners therefore beg Leave to (late, that a Grant of £.4,500 Sterling net is requisite to maintain the present Number of Children, and to enable the Governors to carry into Efleft the proposed Plan of Instruction: And therefore praying the Aid of Parliament for the Support and Advancement of the Mcalurcs necesiary for the full Attainment of the valuable Object of this Institution, founded by Royal Charter, and which subsists almost entirely upon the accustomed and Annual Bounty of Parliament.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table/

and that every Article which constitutes the Funds of this Institution is precarious and uncertain (except £. 50 arising from Government Debentures) and estimated to the full Extent, which the Governors think they can with Safety state: And therefore praying for the further Aid of Parliament, towards the Maintenance of the 107 Children now under their Care, for the ensuing Year: That if it should appear expedient to Parliament to extend the Benefit of this Institution, and to enable the Governors to fill their House with the helpleis and interesting Objects, against whom, from the Inadequacy of their Funds, they are now daily obliged to (hut their Door, a further Grant of £. 750 would be necesiary for the Annual Maintenance of the 50 additional Children which the House could contain, besides £. 200 for the Furniture and Clcathing necesiary for them on their Admission; and the Governors beg Leave to observe, that their Expences could not have been included within these Limits, if they had not been assisted by the gratuitous Services of Gentlemen who have exerted themselves in Favour of the Charity.

Mr. Lawrence Hundas reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Persons thereunto subscribir.g, for themselves, and on Behalf of other Proprietors, Tenants, and Occupiers of Lands, Houses, and Tenements, in the County of Kent, adjacent to the Great Road leading from Hartford to London, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Turnpike Bills and Paving Bills, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's 'fable: W here the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, cinderInnes, Esquire, being examined, said, That the Great Road leading from Hartford to London is a Part of the Great Line of Road leading from Hover to the Capita! of the Kingdom, and that Foreigners from all Part-, of Europe, and Travellers of every Description, as well as the Petitioners, contribute to its Maintenance; and that the said Road more immediately communicates with tiic populous Towns and Villages of Greenwich, Woolwich , Lewifham, and and Two

of His Majesty's Dock Yards, and Ordnance Warren, the Safety, Convenience, and Accommodation of whose Inhabitants, as well as the numerous Persons connected with the Public Service, ought to be attended to; but . that Robberies, and dreadful Accidents, frequently happen on this Road; and that whilst almost every other Road in the Neighbourhood of London is watched, lighted, and watered, this great Approach to the Capital of the Kingdom from the Continent has been, in these Respects, totally neglected — And the Witness added, That the watching, lighting, and watering certain Parts of the said Road, more particularly from East to

Thomas-a-lVaterings, and guarding the Road leading over Black heath and Shooter's Hill to Welting, would be highly beneficial to the Public, as well as creditable and ornamental to the Capital of the Kingdom.

Wrexham, the same would be a Burthen upon many Persons who do not travel more than that Distance upon the said Road; and the Petitioner conceives* that the Tolls arising from the said Turnpike Gate at Holt would, if properly applied, pay the Interest of all the Debts of the said Turnpike Road, and keep the same in proper Repair: And therefore praying, That the said Clause in the said Bill, for making and repairing the Road branching out of the said Road at Pwll-y-rhyd aforesaid, may not pass into a Law; and that the Petitioner may be heard by his Counsel or Agent.

Mr. Henry Alexander, according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider further of the Supply granted to His Majesty* the Resolutions which the Committee had , directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Five Hundred and Five Thousand Five Hundred and Twenty Pounds Nine Shillings and One Penny, be granted to His Majesty, for paying Interest on sundry Exchequer Bills made out by virtue of several Acts of the 39th, the 39th and 40th, and the 41st Years of the Reign of His present Majesty.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Two Thousand Eight Hundred and Sixty-five Pounds and Fifteen Shillings, be granted to His Majesty, to make good the Money issued to the Secretary to the Commissioners for the Reduction of the National Debt, for Salaries of the Officers, and incidental Expences of the said Commission.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding One Hundred and Forty-four Thousand Six Hundred and Eleven Pounds and Two Shillings, be granted to His Majesty, to make good the Money paid for the Purchase of One-third Part of the Annuity of Nineteen Thousand Pounds payable to the Duke of Richmond, pursuant to an Act of the 39th and 40th Years of His present Majesty's Reign.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Five Hundred Pounds, be granted to His Majesty, to make good the Money paid to the Officers of the Exchequer, for Extra Trouble in making out Exchequer Bills.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Four Hundred Fifty-eight Thousand Five Hundred and Fourteen Pounds Eight Shillings and Seven Pence, be granted to His Majesty, to make good the Money paid to the Bank of England for Discount on Prompt Payments to the Loan and Lottery, granted for the Service of the Year 1801.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Twenty-three Thousand Five Hundred and Sixty-two Pounds Three Shillings and Four Pence, be granted to His Majesty, to make good the Money paid to the Bank of for receiving the Contributions to the Loan, and Subscriptions to the Lottery, for the Service of the Year 1801.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding One Thousand Five Hundred Pounds, be granted to His Majesty, to make good the Money paid for incidental Expences attending the Lottery, for the Service of the Year 1801.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Three Millions, be granted to His Majesty, for paying oft* and discharging the Exchequer Bills made out by virtue of an Act, passed in the last Session of Parliament, intituled, "An Act for " railing the Sum of Three Millions by Loans or Exchequer Bills, for the Service of Great Britain, for the " Year 1801."

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Forty-five Thousand Three Hundred Thirty-two Pounds Seventeen Shillings and Six Pence, be granted to His Majesty, to enable His Majesty to make further Indemnification to the Earl Saint Vincent and Lord Grey, late Commanders in Chief in the West Indies, on Account of Decrees against them in the High Court of Admiralty, for the Detention of American Ships at the Capture of Martinique and other Places in the West Indies.

A Petition of the Mayor and Burgesses of the Borough of Lenne Regis, commonly called King's Lynn, in the County of Norfolk, in Council assembled; was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Acts of Parliament now in force for imposing the Duties on Income, are, in the Opinion of the Petitioners, partial and oppressive: And therefore praying, That the House will be pleated to pass a Bill for repealing the said Acts.

A Petition of the Inhabitants of the Borough of Warwick, was presented to the House, and read , Setting forth, That the Tax upon Income is, in its Operation, unequal, partial, and oppressive, inasmuch as the Incomes of Annuitants, the precarious Fruits of personal Industry, and the Profits of Trade (for the obtaining of which the Capitals employed are often exposed to urn-avoidable Hazard) are rated in the same Manner as Incomes arising from Landed or other permanent Property; and that it is destrudfive of the Morals of the People, by holding out Temptations to Fraud and Perjury; and that the inquisitorial Powers established for its Collection are vexatious, and degrading to Individuals, and utterly repugnant to the Principles of a free Constitution: And therefore praying the House, That the Tax upon Income may be wholly repealed.

And the said Petitions were severally ordered to lie upon the Table.

And therefore praying. That the House will take the Premises into their Consideration, and grant such Relief therein as to them shall leern meet.

A Petition of the Lord Mayor, Aldermen, and Commons, of the City of London, in Common Council assembled.

And then they withdrew.

And the said Petition was read; Setting forth. That the Petitioners, conceiving the Tax upon Income, when fir& pfopoi'cd, to be of a partial and uhcohftitutional Tendency, declared, at that Time, their decided Difap-probation of the Measur; and that the Experience of Three Years has not Only justified that Opinion, but the Evils and Inconveniencies reliilting therefrom have greatly exceeded the Apprehensions they then entertained; and that the Petitioners have hitherto fotborhe to complain to the House of the mahy Grievances they have suffered, trusting that the House, intending this as a temporary Import only, would have embraced the earliest Opportunity of relieving the Nation from so opprefliVe, intolerable, and unprecedented a Mode of Taxation; and that, no Steps havirtg been taken by the House towards the Repeal of the said Tax, the Petitioners beg Leave to fepresent to the House some of the many Evils which have arisen, and which tnuft necessarily relult in a Com-frtercial Country, from the delulive Principle, and the hkrrafling and degrading Operation of such an Import; ttftd that the said TaX, bearing no just Proportion to the Property of Individuals, and making no Discrimination between the Income arising from fluctuating and pre-tarious Sources, and the fixed and permanent Income derived from Landed and Eunded Property, falls with Accumulated and accelerating Force upon the Middle Clafres of Society, who have, during a long and calamitous War, sustained the heaviest Burthens, and lub-Ifiitted to the greatest Deprivations; and that the said Tax, by its Operation on those whose Incomes could bear little or no Diminution, has necessarily occasioned a rapid and excessive Advance on all the Articles of Consumption, and thereby reduced to Poverty and Dirtrels many who have heretofore supported their Families with Comfort and Independence; and that the said Tax, by vesting an arbitrary and inquisitorial Power in the Hands of Commissioners, from whose Decision there is no Appeal, subjects the Petitioners to a degrading and humiliating Difelofure of their private and commercial Transactions, which may be attended with the most fatal Consequences to their Credit and Happiness, is l'ubverfive of that Spirit of Independence so necessary to the Security of a free State, and establishes a dangerous and alarming Innovation upon the genuine Pri nciplesof the British Constitution; and that the said Tux, by 'the Multiplication of Oaths, and the various Inducements it holds out to Evasion and Perjury, tends to destroy all Respect for Morality, and to introduce a total Diiregard to the moil; solemn Obligations; and that, from the Consideration of the Objections both to the Principle and Operation of the said Tax, the Petitioners are decidedly of Opinion, that the Nature of it is such as to preclude all Hope of rendering it just or equitable, either by Amendment or Modification: And therefore praying, That the House will take thel'e Matters into their most serious Consideration, and grant the Petitioners Relief, by an immediate Repeal of the said Tax.

Petition of A Petition of the Inhabitants of the City and Liberty WtSerf of Westminster, whose Names are thereunto subscribed.

for repealing And the said Petition was brought up, and read; income °n Setting forth. That the Petitioners feel themselves heavily opprelfed by the Tax which is charged upon Income, not only by the Nature and Extent of the Burthen itself, but by the vexatious Measures which are employed in its Collection; and that it is destructive of the Confidence which happily subsisted among the People, as well as of their Morals, by the Temptation which it holds out to Misrepresentation and Perjury, while, by the Check on private Credit, it dries up the Sources of Industry and Trade; and that its Tendency has been, by its peculiar. Nature, more than that of any other Tax, to advance the Price of all the Necessaries of Life, as well as of all the Materials of Manufacture, and that, though it has been inefficient to the Object for which it was imposed, it has been most afflicting, and even intolerable, in its Operation; and that a Tax, which requires the most rigorous secret Inquisition into the private Affairs of the Subjects of these Kingdoms as ' the M c".ns of Collection, cannot be made compatible with ti:e Spirit and Practice of Constitution;

and the Petitioners conceive that no Modification of furli a Principle can reconcile it with their Rights and P:vileges: And therefore praying the House to take the several ACb, charging a Duty upon Income, into th 'ir Consideration; and that they will be pleased to rcpr.'.i the lame.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Sir, Malta, 18th January 1802.

I have been honoured with your Letter of the 14th November, inclosing the unanimous Resolutions of the House of Commons, of the 12th of that Month, exprefi five of their Thanks to me, to Rear Admirals Sir Richard Bicker ton and Sir John Boriafe Warren, and to the Captains and Officers of the Fleet under my Command, for our Services on the Coast of Egypt; and also the House's Approbation and Acknowdedgment of the Services of the Seamen and Marines on Board the Ships and Vessels under my Command, and under that of Vice Admiral Rainier, which have been communicated by me to Rear-Admiral Sir Richard Bickertony and to such of the Captains, Officers, Seamen, and Marines of the Fleet, who were employed on the Services referred to, as are now here; and I request that you will be pleased to assure the Honourable House, that this repeated Testimony of their Approbation is held by us all in distinguished Esteem.

A Petition of the Inhabitants of the Ward of Castle Baynard, in the City of London, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That, in the Opinion of the Petitioners, the exilting Income Tax is, in its Principle, contrary to the free Spirit of the" Constitution, abhorrent to the Temper of the People, de-

grading to their Character, and calculated, by its Operation, to tread down and destroy those Distinctions which have hitherto been held as the sacred Land Marks between a free and an absolute Government; the Tax has proved, in Practice, more odious, if poffble, than the Principle which gave it Birth; it can Only be effectual in Proportion as it is inquisitorial; its Success depends upon the Degree in which it violates the Confidence of private Life; it puts Englishmen upon Interrogatories as to the various Items of their Acquisi-tions, and Particulars of their Expences, before Persons, who may arbitrarily indulge the most wanton, idle, or interested Curiosity, at the Expence of the Feelings, or the Commercial Advantage, of the Persons thus feru-tinized, who mull either submit to the Surcharges of the Assessors, or expose to Publicity and vulgar Observation the Secrets of their Commerce, and the most

A Petition of the Inhabitants of the City of Hereford, convened by public Advertisement from the Mayor, and held in the Town Hall of the said City, was also presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners, sensibly affected by the Burthens which the calamitous State of Europe has imposed upon this Country, and grateful for the Blessmgs of returning Peace, which His Majesty's present Ministers have laboured to effect, do implore the Houl'c to take into their Consideration the Repeal or Modification of the Tax upon Income; a Tax, which the painful Emergencies of the State at one Time demanded, though the Petitioners were llattered with the Hope that its Operation -would be but temporary; under this Consolation, the Petitioners have cheerfully borne the Pressure of its Effect; and, in Confidence that their Grievances, in common with their Fellow Subjects of the Realm, will ever experience the due Investigation of Parliament, do submit their Petition to the Consideration of the House, arid pray that Relief which it shall think proper to afford.

A Petition of the Commissioners appointed by Act of Parliament, for making wide and convenient Ways, Streets, and Passages in the City of , being

offered to be presented to the House;

Mr Wickham(by His Majesty's Command) acquainted

the House, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth, That being constituted, in the Year 1757, for the Purposes aforesaid, they have been ever since engaged in making Improvements in the City of Dublin, by opening Avenues through the lame, and widening others that were before narrow, confined, and dangerous, and that the several Improvements which they have undertaken have been always previously submitted to, and approved of by Parliament; and that, having no permanent Funds allotted to them before the Year 1782, the Expences incurred by them were, until that Time, supplied by King's letters, or Parliamentary Grants; and that the Funds then allotted them being appropriated, in the first Instance, to the Opening of Dame Street, to the Houses of Parliament, which Work is not yet completed. Parliament have since, when they approved of any new Undertakings, made Grants of Money, from Time to Time, to carry them into Execution; and that these Grants, however, not being equal to the Expences incurred, considerable Debts have been contracted, which have either been discharged by Parliament, or Grants made each Year to defray the Interest of such Debts; and that, for some Years past, they have had, every Session, a Grant of £.4,500 for that Purpose; and that they are now engaged in several Works, by Direction of Acts of Parliament, which their present Funds are not adequate to, and which therefore require either Grants of considerable Sums of Money, or of Funds by new Taxes, on which they may be enabled to borrow Money; and that, by an Act of the 39th George III. they are enjoined to impannel Juries within a Year, to value certain Premises on the South Side the River Liffey, which Juries are still fitting; and that Parliament granted certain Duties to defray the Expences of the Awards of l'uch Juries, and to pay the Intcrelt of the Awards then made; and that the Interest of the said Awards at that Time made exceeds the Prut luce of the Taxes granted by £.625,

independent of £. 1,200 a Year parable to ‘Trinity College,

Dublin, and £.520 a Year to the Bishop of And therefore praying the Hoc e to take the Premises into Consideration, and grant to the Petitioners a Sunt for Payment of the former Interest due, together with such other Sum or Sums of Money, or local Taxes, to enable the Petitioners to raile Money to carry into Execution the Improvements committed to their Care by this Act, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the Mayor, and other Inhabitants of the Borough of King's Lynn, in the County of Norfolk, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioners, with the rest of their Fellow Subjects, finding themselves much aggrieved by the very unequal and oppressive Tax upon Income, and by the vexatious Regulations and Operation thereof, after Three Years Experience, beg Leave to represent the same to the House; and if the Petitioners omit particularly stating the partial Effects thereof, it is because they would not hurt the Feelings of the House, being well allured that the House are fully sensible of the Arguments which might justly be made use of to induce them to repeal the fame: And therefore praying the House will take the said Income Tax into their serious Consideration, and grant the Petitioners Relief, by an immediate Repeal thereof.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Mr. Henry Alexander, according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to ednfider further of Ways and Means for raising the Supply granted to His Majesty, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards railing the Supply granted to His Majesty, the Sum of Twenty-five Millions be raised by Annuities, whereof the Charges of Twenty-three Millions are to be defrayed on the Part of Great , and of Two Millions on the Part of Ireland.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That every Contributor to the said Sum of Twenty-five Millions shall, for every One Hundred Pounds contributed and paid, be entitled to the Principal Sum of Sixty-five Pounds, in Annuities, after the Rate of £. 3 per Centum, to commence from the 5 th Day of January 1802, and to be added to, and made one Joint Stock with, the £. 3 per Centum Annuities consolidated by the Acts of the 25th, 28th, 29th, 32d, and 33d Years of the Reign of his late Majesty King the Second, and by several subsequent Acts, and to be payable and transferable at the Bank of England, at the same Time and in the same Manner, and subject to the like Redemption, as the said £. 3 per Centum Consolidated Annuities.

That every such Contributor shall likewise be entitled to the further Principal Sum of Six Pounds Ninteen Shillings and Three Pence, in the like f. 3 per Centum Annuities, to commence from the 5th Day of January 1808, and then to be added to and made Part of the said £. 3 per Centum Annuities.

That every such Contributor Hull likewise be entitled to the further Principal Sum of Sixty Pounds in Annuities, after the Rate of £. 3 per Centum, to commence from the 5th Day of April 1802, and to be added to, and made one Joint Stock with, certain Annuities, after the Rate of £. 3 per Centum, which were reduced from £. 4 to £. 3 per Centum, by an Act, made in the 23d Year of the Reign of his late Majesty, and to be payable and transferable at the Bank of England, at the same Time and in the same Manner, and subject to the like Redemption by Parliament, as the said f. 3 per Centum Reduced Annuities.

That the said several Annuities, so to be payable as aforesaid, shall be charged and chargeable upon, and payable out of, the Consolidated Fund of Great Britain, or any other Duties and Revenues, which shall be appropriated for that Purpose by any Act or Acts of this prefen t Session of Parliament.

That every Contributor shall, on or before the 14th Day of this Instant April, make a Deposit of 10 per Centum on such Sum as he or she shall chule to subscribe towards raising the said Sum of Twenty-five Millions,

That, towards railing the Supply granted to His Majesty, there be charged upon every Person who shall retain and employ any Male Servant or Servants within Great Britain (except Servants retained or employed solely for the Purpose of Husbandry or Manufactures, or of any Trade or Calling by which the Matter or Mistress of such Servants earn a Livelihood) the several additional Yearly Sums following; that is to say: For One Male Servant, the Sum of Ten Shillings; for Two Male Servants, the Sum of Eight Shillings each; for Three Male Servants, the Sum of Six Shillings each; for Four Male Servants, the Sum of Sixteen Shillings each; for Five Male Servants, the Sum of Fourteen Shillings each; for Six Male Servants, the Sum of Eighteen Shillings each; for Seven Male Servants, the Sum of One Pound each; for Eight Male Servants, the Sum of One Pound each; for Nine Male Servants, the Sum of One Pound and Two Shillings each; for Ten Male Servants, the Sum of One Pound and Six Shillings each; and for Eleven Male Servants, and upwards, the Sum of One Pound and Ten Shillings each.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards railing the Supply granted to His Majesty, every Person carrying on any Trade, Manufacture, or Calling, by which he or she shall earn a Livelihood or Profit, and every Person occupying Lands as the Tenant thereof, and respectively retaining and keeping any Male Servant or Servants, bona fide for the Purposes of such Trade, Manufacture, Calling, or Occupation, who shall lodge or board with his Matter or Mistress, and shall not be employed in any of the Capacities mentioned in an Act, passed in the Twenty-fifth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, shall be charged, for each such Servant, the Yearly Sum of Ten Shillings.

Carriages. Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards raising the Supply granted to His Majesty, every Person who shall keep any Coach, Berlin, landau, Chariot, Calash, Chaifc, Marine Chaise, with Four Wheels, or Caravan, or any Number thereof, for his or her own Use, or to let out to Hire, shall be charged with the several additional Yearly Sums following; that is to say: One such Carriage, and no more, the Sum of Eight Shillings for such Carriage; Two such Carriages, and no more, the Sum of Sixteen Shillings for each; Three such Carriages, and no more, the Sum of Sixteen Shillings for each; Four such Carriages, and no more, the Sum of One Pound Two Shillings for each; Five such Carriages, and no more, the Sum of One Pound Nine Shillings for each; Six such Carriages, and no more, the Sum of One Pound Eighteen Shillings for each; Seven such Carriages, and no more, the Sum of Two Pounds Six Shillings and Sixpence for each; Eight such Carriages, and no more, the Sum of Two Pounds Sixteen Shillings for each; and Nine such Carriages, or more, the Sum of Three Pounds Six Shillings for each.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, the several Act s made in the 15th, 16th, 19th, 20th, and 28th Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, for better regulating the Pipe Water of the City of were read: — And,

Mr. John Carleton being examined, laid, That since the passing of the said Acts, the said City has been increasing in Extent, and has of late Years considerably extended to the Northward and Eastward, and to a great Distance from the present Bason or Reservoir, for supplying the said City with Pipe Water: That the Works to supply the same have been necefi'arily extended, at a great additional Expence, which the present high Rates of Labour, Prices oi Timber, and other Materials, have greatly increased: That the Rates which the Petitioners arc, by the said recited Acts, empowered to receive, have been found so inadequate to the Expences attending the keeping of the said Works in Repair, that the Petitioners have sustained an Annual Lois of about £. 1,200, and muff, in futurej sustain even a more considerable Loss, unless the House shall be pleased to increase the Rates, so as to meet the necessary Expences of the said Establishment. — And the Witness further said. That many Parts to which the City has lately extended are so remote from the present Source from which the said City is served with Water, and lo elevated, that it is with great Difficulty the Inhabitants of those Parts are even partially l'upplied with Water, and cannot be effectually supplied unless the Petitioners are enabled to extend their Works beyond their present Limits.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for amending, altering, and extending, the Powers of the several Acts of Parliament now in Force, for supplying the City of Dublin with Water, and for making better Provision for that Purpose: And that Mr. Beresford, Mr. Foster, Mr. Ogle, and Mr. John Claudius Beresford, do prepare, and bring in, the lame.

Then,

Mr. George Burn being examined, said, That the several Persons possessed of the Mortgages so granted by the said Trustees on the Credit of the said Rates or Duties, are willing and delirous to become Members of such Company, and that the several Sums due to them on such Mortgages should be made Part of the Capital Stock of the said Company; and that several other Persons are willing and delirous to subscribe towards railing a Sum sufficient for carrying into Effect the good Purposes of the said Act, by a Company of Proprietors.

1 have been favoured with your Letter of the 7th Instant, transmitting the unanimous Vote of Thanks of the Honourable House of Commons of the United Parliament of Great Britain and Ireland to the Officers of the Navy, Army, and Marines, for their meritorious Services during the Course of the War; and desiring that the unanimous Resolution of the House, signifying the high Approbation and Acknowledgement of the Services of the Petty and Non-commissioned Officers and Men em- . ployed in His Majesty's Navy, Army, and Marines, may be communicated to them, with Thanks for their exemplary and gallant Behav iour — and in expressing to you the perfect Sense I entertain of the flattering Manner in which you have been pie a fed to communicate the Commands of the House, I requell that the House may be allured, that it is a Circumstance of Angular Satisfaction to me to have to make known to the Army so honourable a Testimony of the meritorious and eminent Services rendered by them to His Majesty and the Nation.

I am, Sir,

Yours,

Right Honourable the Speaker. Frederick.

Mr. Harrison reported from the Committee, to whoni the Petition of the Noblemen, and the humble Petition of the several other Persons, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, on Behalf of themselves and the several other Persons interested in the Lands and Grounds thereinafter mentioned, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Bills of Incloi'ure, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth;

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, passed in the last Session of Parliament, intituled, "An Act for dividing and allotting a certain Fen called " ll'ildmore Fen, in the County of ," by which the Fen was directed to be divided and allotted into Parochial and other General Allotments, was read: — And,

Mr. Robert Clitherozvbeing examined, laid, That it

Would be highly beneficial to the Petitioners, and all others intcrclied in the said lands and Grounds, and of great public Utility, if the Lands and Grounds contained in such Parochial or other General Allotments were l'pccifically divided and allotted in Severalty, to and amongst the several Persons interested, according to their several Rights and Interests therein respectively, the Allotments tnclofed, and the several Tythe Owners compensated for the Tythes thereof; and also, it Provision were made for declaring and determining in what Parishes the same Allotments, and also, the Land authorized to be sold by the Commissioners under the said recited Act, shall be deemed to lie, and be charged to Parochial Dues and Duties. — And the Witness added* That it is apprehended, when the said Lands and Grounds are lo divided, allotted, and inclosed, the same will be inhabited; and that from the great Extent thereof, several of the Inhabitants will be lb far distant from any Church cr Chapel, that it will be necessary to crcft One or more Chapel or Chapels for Divine Worship, and to endow the same with a sufficient Annual Income, out of the said Lands and Grounds, for the Ministers performing Divine Worship therein.

A Petition of the several Inhabitants of the Town and Parish of IValjall, in the County of Stafford, whole Names are thereunto subscribed: And allb,

A Petition of the several Inhabitants of the Town and Parish of Wolverhampton, in the County of whole

Names are thereunto subscribed;

Were severally presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Country for many Miles round them is become very populous, by reason of the Manufactories and very extensive Collieries, Iron Works, and Lime Works, established and carried on therein; and that such Manufactories, Collieries, Iron Works, and Lime Works, have of late Years greatly increased, and are daily very rapidly increasing, and many Miners, Artificers, Workmen, and Labourers, are constantly wanted or employed in the different Mines, Works, and Manufactories; and that, for some Years pall, the Practice of Bull-baiting hath prevailed amongst the lower ClaU'es of Society in the Neighbourhood, in a very alarming Degree, to the great Prejudice of the Persons concerned therein, the Distress, and sometimes the Ruin, of

their respective Families, and to the great Annoyance and Injury of the Public at large; and that such Practice is usually promoted and encouraged by Persons notorious for their Depravity; and Drunkenness, idleness. Gaming,

Swearing, and every other Species of Disorder and Riot, are the Consequences of itr, and it is become highly offensive to all peaceable and well-disposed Persons: And therefore praying, That the House will adopt such Measures to redress this growing Evil, as to them shall seem meet.

And the said Petitions were severally ordered to lie upon the Table.

And the said Clause was Twice read; and, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House, to be made Part of the Bill.

Ordered, That the Bill, with the Amendments, be ingrossed.

Ordered, That the said Bill be read the Third Time Tomorrow Morning, if the said Bill shall be then ingrafted.

Sir John Honywood reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the several Persons, w'hose Names are thereunto subscribed, being Commissioners for executing Two Acts, passed for paving, cleansing, lighting, and otherwise improving, the Town of in the County of Kent, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Paving Bills, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the lame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read} and is as follow'eth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, an Act, passed in the 31st Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for widening, improving, regulating, paving, cleansing, and lighting the Streets, Lanes, and other public Railages and Places, within the King's Town of Maidstone, in the County of Kent 5 for removing and

preventing Encroachments, Obstructions, Nuisances, and Annoyances therein} for better supplying the said Town with Water} and for repairing the Highways within the Parish of Maidstone; and also, an Act, passed in the

36th Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for enabling the Commissioners for executing the above-mentioned Act, to raise a further Sum of Money for completing the Purposes of the said Act, were read: —

Then,

Mr. George Burr being examined, laid. That, by the first-mentioned Act, the Commissioners appointed to put the same in Execution, are authorized to borrow, on the Credit of the Rates thereby granted, a Sum not exceeding £.7,000, for the more expeditious Performance of the several intended Improvements} that the Commissioners have proceeded to execute the said Act, and have made great Progress therein, for which Purpose they have borrowed and expended the Whole of the said Sum, and have also incurred several considerable Debts, which they have no Means of discharging, nor are they able to carry the Purposes of the said Act into complete Effect, without further Powers. — And the Witness being further examined, laid, That the Commissioners have endeavoured to borrow a further Sum of Money under the Authority of the said last-recited Act, but have not been able to procure any, the Rates which they are now authorized to impose by the said first-recited Act, not being sufficient to induce Persons to lend any more Money on the Credit thereof; that the said Improvements of the said Town cannot be completed, nor the said Debt lb incurred be paid oil', unless Power is given to raise a further Sum of Money for that Purpose, and also to increase the said Rates; that all Persons relbrting to, or passing through the said Town, with Cattle and Carriages, receive material Convenience and Advantage from the paving and improving of the said Streets; and that the Petitioners conceive that such Persons should contribute towards the Expence thereof, by the Payment of Toll, or in such other Manner as Parliament may think proper; and that the Powers and ProvisionB of the said Acts have also been found defective in other Respects.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for altering and amending an Act, passed in the 31st Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled,
